definition_zh: 根虫；取食植物根部的甲虫幼虫
definition_en: a beetle larva that feeds on the roots of plants, especially of maize
core_image: 泥土里一条白色幼虫正把玉米的根须咬断
scene: 农技员蹲在田边，轻轻扒开一株玉米根部的泥土，查看白嫩的虫子有没有啃坏根须。The agronomist pushed back the soil around a maize stalk to check whether rootworms had eaten into its roots.
sceneCN: 这里 rootworm 是「根虫」（第 1 个义项：在植物根部取食的甲虫幼虫）；句意：农技员拨开一株玉米根部的泥土，查看根虫是否已经啃进根系。

collocations.zh: 玉米根萤叶甲（俗称玉米根虫）
根虫抗性（作物对根虫的抗性）

derivatives.zh: 根；根部，是复合词的前半部分，点明危害发生的部位
虫；蠕虫，是复合词的后半部分，泛指长身软体的昆虫幼虫
rootworm 加复数后缀构成，指多个虫体，常用于监测报告

senses.title: A larva that eats plant roots
senses.definition: the grub or larva of certain leaf beetles that lives in the soil and burrows into the roots of crops
senses.definitionCN: 某些叶甲科甲虫的幼虫，生活于土壤中，钻入作物根部取食
senses.example: Rootworms were found below the surface of the wheat field.
senses.exampleCN: 人们在小麦田的地下发现了根虫。
senses.why: The compound simply joins root and worm, and names the larva by where it lives and feeds.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「根」和「虫」直接复合而成，用幼虫生活和取食的部位来给它命名。

senses.title: The maize pest in particular
senses.definition: in agriculture the north American corn rootworm, whose larvae attack maize roots and reduce the harvest
senses.definitionCN: 农业上多指北美的玉米根萤叶甲，其幼虫啃食玉米根系，造成减产
senses.example: Corn rootworm is one of the most costly pests in the Midwest.
senses.exampleCN: 玉米根萤叶甲是美国中西部损失最惨重的害虫之一。
senses.why: Because maize is its main host, the general worm-name has narrowed to one notorious species in farming talk.
senses.whyCN: 因为玉米是它的主要寄主，日常农事用语里这个泛称就专门指那种臭名昭著的害虫。

senses.title: The damage it leaves behind
senses.definition: the injury itself, such as chewed roots and lodged stalks in a field
senses.definitionCN: 指根虫造成的伤害本身，例如被啃坏的根系和倒伏的茎秆
senses.example: Rootworm damage showed up as plants falling over after a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 一场暴风雨后植株倒伏，就是根虫危害的表现。
senses.why: Since the pest is named for its effect on roots, farmers often use the word for the visible loss rather than the insect.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种虫是按它对根系的作用得名的，农户常直接用该词指看得见的损失，而不指昆虫本身。

senses.title: A name in plant breeding
senses.definition: a label used in crop breeding and pest control, as in traits that make plants resistant to the insect
senses.definitionCN: 作物育种和害虫防治中的标签，如使作物对该昆虫具有抗性的性状
senses.example: Breeders have developed hybrids with rootworm resistance.
senses.exampleCN: 育种家已经培育出具有根虫抗性的杂交种。
senses.why: Once a pest is a key enemy, its name becomes a standard term for resistance, tolerance and control programmes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某种害虫成为主要敌人，它的名字就会变成抗性、耐受性和防治方案的固定术语。

senses.title: The adult alongside the larva
senses.definition: in loose field use, the yellow-green adult beetle of the same species that feeds on leaves and silk
senses.definitionCN: 在田间口语中也可泛指同物种的黄绿色成虫，成虫啃食叶片和玉米须
senses.example: Growers monitor rootworm adults in late summer.
senses.exampleCN: 种植者在夏末监测根虫成虫的数量。
senses.why: Strictly the word describes the larva, but people often transfer the common name to the whole life cycle.
senses.whyCN: 严格来说这个词指幼虫，但人们常把俗称连带用于整个生命周期中的成虫。

senses.title: A model for resistance
senses.definition: the insect as a widely cited case of pests evolving resistance to genetically engineered maize
senses.definitionCN: 这种昆虫被广泛引为害虫对转基因玉米演化出抗性的典型案例
senses.example: Rootworm resistance has already appeared in several states.
senses.exampleCN: 根虫的抗药性已经在好几个州出现。
senses.why: Repeated exposure to one kind of crop or chemical makes the pest a textbook example of adaptation.
senses.whyCN: 长期单一地接触某种作物或药剂，让这种害虫成了「适应性演化」的教科书案例。

senses.title: Root-feeding pests in general
senses.definition: extended in garden and horticultural writing to similar worms that attack the roots of other crops
senses.definitionCN: 在园艺写作中引申泛指啃食其他作物根部的类似蠕虫
senses.example: Gardeners in the region call almost any pale soil grub a rootworm.
senses.exampleCN: 当地园丁几乎把任何浅色的土栖幼虫都叫作根虫。
senses.why: The transparent shape of the compound lets speakers extend it to any pale worm-like larva found among roots.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词构成明白易懂，所以可以顺延指任何在根间发现的浅色蠕虫状幼虫。

intro.en: Rootworm is an English compound of root and worm. Root comes from Old English rot, and worm from Old English wyrm; the combination names a grub that eats farm roots.
intro.cn: rootworm 是英语复合词，由 root（根）和 worm（虫）组成。root 源自古英语 rot，worm 源自古英语 wyrm，组合起来指啃食作物根部的幼虫。

items.en: Reconstructed wrōts means a root, and wurmiz means a snake or creeping thing.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式 wrōts 意为「根」，wurmiz 意为「蛇、蠕虫」。

items.en: Rot is the root of a plant, and wyrm is a snake or worm.
items.cn: 古英语 rot 指植物的根，wyrm 指蛇或虫。

items.en: Worm covers snakes, dragons and any creeping creature.
items.cn: 中古英语中 worm 可指蛇、龙以及一切攀爬或蠕动的生物。

items.en: The general sense shifts to the larvae and grubs that infest crops.
items.cn: 英语词义转向危害农作物的幼虫与蛴螬。

items.en: Root-worm names the corn pest, with corn rootworm as the standard form.
items.cn: 美式英语中用 root-worm 指玉米害虫，corn rootworm 成为标准说法。

items.en: Modern spelling rootworm appears in pest management and patent documents.
items.cn: 现代拼写 rootworm 常见于害虫管理与专利文献。

note.en: Rootworm is close in form to root words and in meaning to pests and worms that live in soil or feed on plants.
note.cn: rootworm 在形式上接近含 root 的复合词，在意义上接近土壤害虫和取食植物的蠕虫类词。

entries.definition: the part of a plant that grows underground
a long soft-bodied animal, or a creeping larva
a type of worm with a rounded, unsegmented body
entries.definitionCN: 线虫，只是拼写相近且同为虫名，词源不同

entries.definition: a thick worm-like beetle larva that lives in the soil
the hard-bodied larva of a click beetle that damages roots
entries.definitionCN: 金针虫，叩甲幼虫，会危害根部

entries.definition: a tiny worm-like pest of roots and soil
entries.definitionCN: 线虫，土中微小的根害虫

normalIntro.en: Rootworm is a transparent compound: a worm that lives in and eats roots.
normalIntro.cn: rootworm 是一个一眼就能看懂的复合词：住在根里、吃根的虫。

normal.en: Root plus worm names the pest by the part it attacks.
normal.cn: root 加 worm，按它攻击的部位来命名。

normal.en: Corn rootworm is the most common long form in farming.
normal.cn: 在农业中 corn rootworm 是最常见的完整说法。

normal.en: The plural is simply rootworms.
normal.cn: 复数只需直接加 -s 写成 rootworms。

normal.en: Breeding and control talk about rootworm resistance.
normal.cn: 育种与防治中常说 rootworm resistance（根虫抗性）。

normal.en: Compare wireworm and nematode, which are other root pests.
normal.cn: 可对比 wireworm 与 nematode，它们也是根部害虫。

abstract.en: Picture a pale larva curled around a tangled maize root.
abstract.cn: 想象一条苍白的幼虫蜷绕在盘结的玉米根上。

abstract.en: See a whole field of tall stalks leaning after a storm.
abstract.cn: 想象暴风雨后整片高秆玉米歪斜倒伏。

abstract.en: Think of a beetle whose name is borrowed for a whole research field.
abstract.cn: 想象一种甲虫的名字被借去命名整个研究领域。

examples.en: Rootworms live in the soil and bore into the roots of maize.
examples.cn: 根虫生活在土壤里，会钻进玉米根部。

examples.en: Crop rotation helps farmers keep corn rootworm numbers down.
examples.cn: 轮作有助于农户压低玉米根虫的数量。

examples.en: The seed is bred with genes for rootworm resistance.
examples.cn: 这种种子经过培育，带有根虫抗性基因。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「入土虫」——钻入土里啃根的虫；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: root（根，古英语 rot）＋ worm（虫，古英语 wyrm）→ 英语复合词 rootworm／root-worm → 特指玉米根萤叶甲等根部害虫，核心义「在根部取食的虫」。

sensesIntro.en: Rootworm starts from the literal soil larva, narrows to the maize pest, then extends to the damage, the breeding term, the adult and the general idea of a resistance case.
sensesIntro.cn: rootworm 先指土里取食根部的幼虫，再窄指玉米害虫，然后延伸到危害、育种术语、成虫以及抗性典型案例等用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale larva gnawing the roots of a maize stalk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条苍白的幼虫在啃玉米的根。

branches.en: The literal larva in the soil is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 土中取食根部的幼虫是基础义项。

branches.en: Maize pests are the narrow agricultural sense.
branches.cn: 玉米根虫是收窄后的农业义项。

branches.en: The injury itself is the result sense.
branches.cn: 危害本身是结果义项。

branches.en: Breeding terms and resistance cases grow from the pest name.
branches.cn: 育种术语与抗性案例都从害虫名生长出来。

branches.en: The adult insect and other root pests are extensions of the label.
branches.cn: 成虫与其他根部害虫是这一标签的延伸用法。

intro.en: Rootworm is a two-part English compound. Its halves are both native words with long lives in the language.
intro.cn: rootworm 是英语两部分复合词，两部分都是历史悠久的本族词。

latinIntro.en: Neither half comes from Latin directly, but English keeps Latin scientific names such as Diabrotica for the same insects.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不是直接来自拉丁语，但英语沿用拉丁学名来描述同一类昆虫，例如 Diabrotica。

definition_zh: 讲台；演讲台；（动物的）嘴；喙；（古罗马战舰的）撞角
definition_en: a raised platform for public speaking, or a beak, or the beak-shaped prow of an ancient warship
core_image: 一根鸟喙高高伸起，人站在它上面向人群讲话
scene: 典礼上，主持人走上高出的木台，示意大家安静，台下几百双眼睛望着她。The host stepped up onto the rostrum and raised one hand to quiet the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 rostrum 是「讲台」（第 1 个义项：供人在众人面前讲话的高出平台）；句意：主持人走上讲台，举起一只手示意人群安静下来。

derivatives.zh: 加 -al 构成形容词，意为「吻部的；喙部的」，多用于解剖学
加 -ate 构成形容词，意为「有喙的；喙状的」，用于植物与动物描述
加指小词尾 -ellum 构成的指小形式，指小而像喙的结构
rostrum 加 -form（形状）构成，意为「喙形的」

senses.title: A platform for public speaking
senses.definition: a raised stand from which a speaker addresses an audience, such as a platform at a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 演讲者面向听众讲话的高出一层的台子，如典礼上的台座
senses.example: She walked to the rostrum and waited for silence.
senses.exampleCN: 她走到讲台前，等待全场安静。
senses.why: Roman orators spoke from a platform decorated with ships beaks, so the beaked structure gave its name to the speakers stand.
senses.whyCN: 古罗马演说家站在装饰着船首撞角的高台上讲话，那个「喙状」的结构便把名字借给了讲台。

senses.title: Beak or snout
senses.definition: the beak of a bird or the long snout of certain fish, insects and mammals
senses.definitionCN: 鸟的喙，或某些鱼、昆虫、哺乳动物长长的嘴部
senses.example: The heron uses its rostrum to spear small fish.
senses.exampleCN: 鹭用它长长的喙刺取小鱼。
senses.why: Latin rostrum means a beak, and that is the oldest and most literal sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rostrum 本义就是「喙」，这是该词最古老、最字面的义项。

senses.title: The beak of a warship
senses.definition: an iron beak-like spur on the prow of an ancient warship, used to ram enemy vessels
senses.definitionCN: 古代战舰船首像鸟喙一样伸出的铁制撞角，用来撞击敌船
senses.example: The galley struck with its bronze rostrum.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘桨帆船用青铜撞角撞了上去。
senses.why: Because the ram looked like a beak, the same word named the weapon, and the decorated platform of Roman speakers.
senses.whyCN: 因为撞角形状像鸟喙，同一个词既指这件武器，又指罗马演说家所站的装饰平台。

senses.title: A speaker s platform in debate
senses.definition: the specific raised desk or stand from which a member speaks in a parliament or debating society
senses.definitionCN: 议会或辩论社团中成员发言所用的高出声台
senses.example: The minister was called back to the rostrum for a second question.
senses.exampleCN: 部长被叫回发言台回答第二个问题。
senses.why: The ceremonial sense narrows further into the fixed furniture of parliaments and congress halls.
senses.whyCN: 仪典义进一步收窄为议会与大会堂中固定的发言台设施。

senses.title: A public mouthpiece
senses.definition: figurative use for the public stage where opinions are voiced, as in a debate or campaign
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性的用法，指公开发表意见的舞台，如辩论或竞选场合
senses.example: The scandal moved from court records onto the public rostrum.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩丑闻从法庭卷宗进入了公开的舆论讲台。
senses.why: Once the platform stands for public speech, the word can stand for any open venue of argument.
senses.whyCN: 当讲台代表公开言论之后，这个词就可以代表任何公开辩论的场合。

senses.title: A mouthpart in zoology
senses.definition: an elongated structure at the front of an animal, such as the piercing mouthparts of a bug
senses.definitionCN: 动物身体前端延长的结构，如某些昆虫用来刺吸的口器
senses.example: Under the microscope, the rostrum of the bug is clearly a hollow tube.
senses.exampleCN: 在显微镜下，那只虫的喙显然是中空的管。
senses.why: Scientific Latin extends the beak sense to any elongated front part of an organism.
senses.whyCN: 科学拉丁语把「喙」的义项扩展到生物体任何延长的前端结构。

senses.title: The ship wreckage among monuments
senses.definition: in classical studies, one of the captured ship beaks once displayed as war trophies on the Roman forum
senses.definitionCN: 古典学中指曾作为战利品陈列在罗马广场上的缴获船首撞角
senses.example: Historians link the column to the rostra of captured ships.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把这根纪念柱与被俘船只的撞角联系起来。
senses.why: The historical sense returns to the concrete object after centuries of naming the platform above it.
senses.whyCN: 这个历史义项回到了具体实物本身，虽然这个词已经指它上方的平台好几百年了。

intro.en: Rostrum is Latin for a beak. In Roman times the speaks platform in the forum was hung with captured ship beaks, so the word shifted from the beaks to the platform itself.
intro.cn: rostrum 是拉丁语「喙」的意思。古罗马广场上的演讲台曾挂满缴获的敌船撞角，于是这个词从撞角转指讲台本身。

items.en: Rostrum means a beak, snout or prow, from rodere, to gnaw.
items.cn: rostrum 意为喙、口鼻或船首，源自 rodere（啃咬）。

items.en: The Rostra in the Roman forum is decorated with captured ship beaks.
items.cn: 罗马广场的演说台以缴获的船首撞角装饰得名。

items.en: Rostra, the plural, becomes the usual name for the speakers platform.
items.cn: 复数形式 rostra 成为演讲台的常用称呼。

items.en: Rostrum enters English for a speakers standing place.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 rostrum，指演说者站立的台子。

items.en: The word also keeps its Latin beak sense in zoology.
items.cn: 现代英语在动物学中保留其拉丁语「喙」的义项。

note.en: Rostrum is close in form to its Latin family, and in meaning to stage, podium and beak.
note.cn: rostrum 在形式上接近它的拉丁词族，在意义上接近 stage、podium 与 beak。

having a beak
a small beak-like part on an orchid or tapeworm
entries.definitionCN: 兰科植物或绦虫头部的小喙状结构

entries.definition: a small platform for a speaker or conductor

normalIntro.en: Rostrum is a beak that became a platform: think of a giant beak standing in a square with speakers on top.
normalIntro.cn: rostrum 是「喙」变成的「台子」：想象广场中立着一根巨大的鸟喙，演说者站在上面。

normal.en: The Latin root rodere means to gnaw, and rostrum means the beak that does the gnawing.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 rodere 意为啃咬，rostrum 就是用来啃咬的喙。

normal.en: Rostral and rostrate are the two common adjectives from it.
normal.cn: 由它构成的常见形容词是 rostral 与 rostrate。

normal.en: The plural is rostra, and the English plural rostrums also appears.
normal.cn: 复数一般写作 rostra，英式化写法 rostrums 也可用。

normal.en: Step up to the rostrum is a formal way to say go and speak.
normal.cn: step up to the rostrum 是「上台发言」的正式说法。

normal.en: Compare podium, which is a narrow stand for one speaker.
normal.cn: 可对比 podium，它指供单人使用的窄台。

abstract.en: Picture a bronze beak from a sunken ship nailed to a stone platform.
abstract.cn: 想象一块从沉船上取下的青铜撞角钉在石台上。

abstract.en: Imagine a heron standing on one leg and pointing its long beak at you.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鹭单腿站立，长长的喙正对着你。

abstract.en: Think of a debate where arguments fly like the prows of warships.
abstract.cn: 想象一场辩论，观点像战舰的船首一样互相冲撞。

examples.en: The speaker climbed onto the rostrum and began to read.
examples.cn: 演讲者登上讲台，开始朗读。

examples.en: Rostra of captured warships once lined the Roman forum.
examples.cn: 罗马广场上曾经排满缴获战舰的船首撞角。

examples.en: The bird has a straight, sharp rostrum for catching fish.
examples.cn: 这种鸟长着笔直而尖锐的喙，用来捕鱼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「若思吹」——站上讲台，要想清楚再吹牛；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rodere（啃咬）→ rostrum（喙）→ 罗马广场演说台的撞角装饰 rostra → 英语 rostrum（讲台），核心义「向前伸出的喙」。

sensesIntro.en: Rostrum moves from the literal beak, to the beak of a warship, to the trophy-covered platform, and finally to platforms and public speech.
sensesIntro.cn: rostrum 从字面的鸟喙，到战舰撞角，再到挂满战利品的演说台，最后转为讲台与公开发言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird beak jutting forward over a listening crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根向前伸出的鸟喙悬在听众头顶。

branches.en: The speaker platform is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 讲话的台子是日常义项。

branches.en: The beak itself keeps the oldest sense alive.
branches.cn: 鸟喙本身保留着最古老的义项。

branches.en: War trophies and their display connect the ship and the platform.
branches.cn: 战利品及其陈列把战舰与讲台连在一起。

branches.en: Parliament desks and public stages are the abstract extensions.
branches.cn: 议会发言台与公开舞台是抽象延伸。

branches.en: Zoology uses the word for any elongated mouthpart.
branches.cn: 动物学用它指任何延长的口器。

intro.en: Rostrum is a whole Latin noun, and its family is built with adjective and diminutive endings rather than prefixes.
intro.cn: rostrum 是一个完整的拉丁名词，它的词族靠形容词词尾与指小词尾构成，而不是靠前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin rostrum means a beak and comes from rodere, to gnaw, which also gives rodent and erosion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rostrum 意为喙，来自 rodere（啃咬），后者也产生了 rodent 与 erosion。

items.example: Rodere supplies the gnawing image behind the beak.
items.exampleCN: rodere 提供了喙背后「啃咬」的意象。

items.meaning: a beak, snout or ship prow
items.example: Rostrum is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: rostrum 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -al forms rostral.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 rostral。

items.example: Rostral is common in anatomy texts.
items.exampleCN: rostral 常见于解剖学文献。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms rostrate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 rostrate。

items.example: The suffix -ellum forms rostellum.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ellum 构成 rostellum。

items.meaning: a small beak, as in an orchid or tapeworm head
items.meaningCN: 小喙，如兰花或绦虫头部的结构
items.example: Rostellum names the small hooked front part.
items.exampleCN: rostellum 指小小的钩状前部。

items.example: The suffix -form forms rostriform.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -form 构成 rostriform。

items.example: Rostrate describes plants and shells.
items.exampleCN: rostrate 用于描述植物与贝壳。

items.example: Rodent keeps the gnawing root of rodere.
items.exampleCN: rodent 保留了 rodere 的「啃咬」词根。

definition_zh: 腐烂；腐朽；（使）腐败；糟透；胡话
definition_en: to decay or become soft and broken down through the action of bacteria and fungi
core_image: 一只木箱在潮气里慢慢发黑、变软、塌下去
scene: 雨下了半个月，仓库角落那只木箱早已变了颜色，轻轻一碰就碎成渣，还散着霉味。Rain had seeped into the warehouse for weeks, and the wooden crate in the corner had begun to rot.
sceneCN: 这里 rot 是「腐烂」（第 1 个义项：有机物因细菌或真菌的作用而变软变坏）；句意：雨水渗进仓库好几个星期，角落里的木箱已经开始腐烂。

collocations.zh: 开始腐朽（比喻风气败坏）

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词 -en 形式或同源形容词而来，意为「腐烂的；糟透的」
三单形式，第三人称单数谓语时的写法
动名词形式，指「腐烂的过程」，如木材腐烂研究

senses.title: To decay and break down
senses.definition: to be destroyed gradually by bacteria and fungi until soft or crumbled, as fruit or wood does
senses.definitionCN: 被细菌和真菌逐渐分解，变得软烂或碎裂，如水果或木头那样
senses.example: Half the apples in the basket had begun to rot.
senses.exampleCN: 篮子里有一半苹果已经开始烂了。
senses.why: The core sense is biological decay, when living tissue loses its hold and turns to slime or dust.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是生物性的腐败：活着的组织失去了结构，变成黏液或碎屑。

senses.title: To make something decay
senses.definition: to cause food, timber or other material to become decayed through wet or damp conditions
senses.definitionCN: 由于潮湿或水汽，使食物、木料或其他材料腐坏
senses.example: Leaking gutters rotted the beams above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 漏水的天沟把门上的横梁腐坏了。
senses.why: The same verb works as a causative: water or neglect does the rotting to the thing.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也可作使役用法：水汽或疏于照管让那东西烂掉。

senses.title: The rotten state
senses.definition: the condition of being decayed, or the decayed material itself
senses.definitionCN: 已经腐坏的状态，或腐坏的物质本身
senses.example: The floor gave way where dry rot had spread.
senses.exampleCN: 干腐蔓延到的地方，地板已经塌陷。
senses.why: A process consumes its result, so the verb becomes the noun that names the decayed stuff.
senses.whyCN: 过程会留下结果，于是动词转为名词，指那腐烂的东西。

senses.title: A moral spiral downward
senses.definition: to become bad or corrupted in a people, society or institution over time
senses.definitionCN: 指人、社会或制度随着时间变坏、腐化
senses.example: Corruption rotted the police from within.
senses.exampleCN: 腐败使警察队伍从内部烂掉。
senses.why: The image of a falling apartment or a spoiled flower readily applies to social fabric.
senses.whyCN: 腐烂的画面能自然套用到社会肌体上：内在一点点坏到骨头里。

senses.title: Nonsense, idle talk
senses.definition: informal word for silly or untrue talk from someone bluffing or exaggerating
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示某人在吹牛或夸张时说的愚蠢、不实的话
senses.example: Do not talk rot: the test has to be run again.
senses.exampleCN: 别胡说，试验必须重做。
senses.why: Rotten thoughts are thought of as decayed thoughts, so nonsense is called by the decay word.
senses.whyCN: 烂掉的想法就是腐坏的想法，于是胡话也用「腐烂」这个词来称呼。

senses.title: Something already spoiled
senses.definition: an item of food, such as fruit or meat, that is unfit to eat because of decay
senses.definitionCN: 因腐烂而不能再吃的食物，如水果或肉
senses.example: Take the rot out of the crate before you sell the rest.
senses.exampleCN: 把烂掉的挑出去，再把其余的好果子卖掉。
senses.why: The noun can count individual affected pieces while keeping the same decayed image.
senses.whyCN: 名词也可以一个个地计数，但保留同一个腐败的画面。

senses.title: Wasting away in a place
senses.definition: informal use for spending time in an unpleasant situation, such as prison, with little hope of change
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法，指在监狱等不愉快环境中度日无所改变
senses.example: He will rot in prison for what he did.
senses.exampleCN: 他犯下的事会让他终老狱中。
senses.why: Time spent rotting in a damp cell is the concrete picture that gave the idiom its emotional force.
senses.whyCN: 在潮湿牢房里腐烂的漫长时光，是这一惯用表达情感力度的具体画面。

intro.en: Rot is an old Germanic word. Old English rotian already meant to decay; the stable noun and the adjective rotten come from the same group.
intro.cn: rot 是古老的日耳曼词。古英语 rotian 就有「腐烂」之义，同名词与形容词 rotten 来自同一词群。

items.en: A reconstructed root rut- or reud- is linked to redness and decay, though the link is debated.
items.cn: 一般认为来自重构形式 rut- 或 reud-，与发红、腐败相联，但这一联系仍有争议。

items.en: Rotian means to decay, and roten means decayed.
items.cn: 古英语 rotian 意为腐烂，roten 意为腐坏的。

items.en: Cognate rotsja keeps the same decay sense in Dutch Frisian.
items.cn: 同源的 rotsja 在荷兰与弗里斯兰语中保留同样的腐烂义。

items.en: Rotten spreads as the usual adjective, and rot appears as a noun.
items.cn: 中古英语中 rotten 成为常用形容词，rot 出现名词用法。

items.en: The verb grows figurative senses, as in rot in prison.
items.cn: 近代英语中动词发展出比喻义，如在狱中腐烂。

items.en: The informal noun of nonsense, as in talk rot, is established.
items.cn: 现代英语确立了口语中表示「胡话」的名词用法，如 talk rot。

note.en: Rot is close in form to its own family of forms, and in meaning to decay and spoil.
note.cn: rot 在形式上接近它自己的词形变化，在意义上接近 decay 与 spoil 这一组词。

entries.definition: decayed and unfit to use
a long thin stick or bar
entries.definitionCN: 杆子；细棒，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a disorderly retreat or defeat
entries.definitionCN: 溃败；败退，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to be gradually destroyed by natural processes
to become unfit to eat
to rot with a foul smell

normalIntro.en: Rot is short and blunt, like the state it names: something that is going soft and dark from the inside.
normalIntro.cn: rot 又短又直，正好对应它所指的状态：东西从里到外慢慢变软、发黑。

normal.en: Old English rotian is the ancestor of the verb.
normal.cn: 古英语 rotian 是这个词的动词祖先。

normal.en: The adjective rotten belongs to the same group.
normal.cn: 形容词 rotten 属于同一词群。

normal.en: Rot away means to be slowly eaten away by decay.
normal.cn: rot away 表示被腐蚀而慢慢消失。

normal.en: Talk rot is a fixed phrase for nonsense.
normal.cn: talk rot 是表示「胡说」的固定说法。

normal.en: Compare spoil and decay, which are close but less vivid for moral contexts.
normal.cn: 可对比 spoil 与 decay：意思相近，但用于道德语境时不如 rot 生动。

abstract.en: Picture a crate whose corner has turned soft and black.
abstract.cn: 想象一只木箱的边角已经变软发黑。

abstract.en: Imagine a knife left in water for a week.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小刀在水里放了整整一星期。

abstract.en: Think of a promise that crumbles the moment it is tested.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺一经考验就碎成渣。

examples.en: The old boat slowly rotted in the damp shed.
examples.cn: 那条旧船在潮湿的棚子里慢慢朽坏了。

examples.en: Fruit begins to rot quickly in summer heat.
examples.cn: 炎热的夏天里水果很快就开始腐烂。

examples.en: Do not talk rot; the plan failed for a reason.
examples.cn: 别胡说了，这个计划失败是有原因的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肉特（软）」——肉放久了特别软，就烂了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 rotian（腐烂）→ 中古英语 roten、rot → 英语 rot（腐烂）→ 引申「腐化、胡说」，核心义「由内向外坏掉」。

sensesIntro.en: Rot begins with natural decay, then covers the cause, the result and the spoiled stuff, and finally spreads to moral corruption and idle talk.
sensesIntro.cn: rot 从自然的腐败出发，再覆盖成因、结果与腐坏之物，最后扩展到道德腐化和胡话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet wooden box going soft and dark at the corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：潮湿的木箱边角变得发软发黑。

branches.en: The biological decay of tissue is the base sense.
branches.cn: 组织的生物性腐败是基础义项。

branches.en: Causing decay shifts the verb into the causative.
branches.cn: 使某物腐坏是使役用法。

branches.en: The state of rot and the spoiled item are noun senses.
branches.cn: 腐烂状态与腐坏之物是名词义项。

branches.en: Corruption transfers decay to people and systems.
branches.cn: 腐化把「腐烂」转移到了人与制度上。

branches.en: Idle talk and wasted time are the colloquial branch.
branches.cn: 胡话与虚度时间是口语分支。

intro.en: Rot is a free English base with little affixing. Its family is built by endings such as -en and -ing.
intro.cn: rot 是能独立使用的英语词基，几乎没有加缀。它的词族靠 -en 与 -ing 等词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Rot has no Latin source; it is a native Germanic word. The Latin neighbour is putrere, to rot, found in putrid and putrefy.
latinIntro.cn: rot 没有拉丁来源，是本族日耳曼词。与它相邻的拉丁语是 putrere（腐烂），见于 putrid 与 putrefy。

items.meaning: to decay, or the decay itself
items.example: Rot names the basic decay.
items.exampleCN: rot 指基本的腐烂现象。

items.example: Rotian is the earliest English form.
items.exampleCN: rotian 是最古老的英语形式。

items.meaning: forming an adjective from a verb
items.meaningCN: 由动词构成形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -en forms rotten.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -en 构成 rotten。

items.meaning: decayed, or of very poor quality
items.example: Rotten is the common adjective.
items.exampleCN: rotten 是常用形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms rotting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 rotting。

items.example: Rotting describes a process in progress.
items.exampleCN: rotting 描述正在进行的腐烂。

items.meaningCN: 构成过去式与过去分词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms rotted.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 rotted。

items.example: Rots is the simple present form.
items.exampleCN: rots 是一般现在时形式。

items.example: Putrid shares the decay meaning from Latin.
items.exampleCN: putrid 来自拉丁语的同一腐烂义。

items.example: Rotted is used as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: rotted 可作形容词使用。

definition_zh: 路由器；刨槽工具；安排路线的人
definition_en: a device that sends data between different networks or machines
core_image: 一个十字路口的小岗亭，把每条消息指向该去的路
scene: 办公室断网时，同事把网线插回了路由器。When the office lost its connection, a colleague plugged the cable back into the router.
sceneCN: 这里 router 是「路由器」（第 1 个义项：在网络与设备之间转发数据的装置）；句意：办公室断网时，同事把网线插回了路由器。

pos.zh: 路由器；路径装置；刨槽工具

derivatives.zh: 路线；路线指引；为……规定路线
路径选择；数据转发；刨槽作业
已为某条路线指定的；被安排路线的
击溃；赶走（与 router 拼写相近，词源不同）

senses.title: A network data forwarder
senses.definition: a device that receives network data and sends it toward its destination
senses.definitionCN: 接收网络数据并把它转发往目标地址的设备
senses.example: The router links the home laptops to the internet.
senses.exampleCN: 路由器把家里的笔记本电脑接入互联网。
senses.why: A router does exactly what its name promises: it works out the route for each packet and passes it along.
senses.whyCN: 路由器做的事正合它的名字：为每个数据包确定路线并转发出去，所以这个义项从「指路」的意象直接长出来。

senses.title: A routing machine in woodworking
senses.definition: a power tool with a spinning cutter that cuts grooves or shapes into wood
senses.definitionCN: 带旋转刀具、能在木材上开槽或成形的电动工具
senses.example: He used a router to cut a groove for the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 他用刨槽机为隔板开了一道槽。
senses.why: The tool guides a cutter along a set path, so it routes the blade through the timber in the same sense the noun routes traffic.
senses.whyCN: 这件工具让刀具沿着既定路径推进，和路由器给数据安排路径是同一动作，因此共用指路义。

senses.title: Someone or something that routes others
senses.definition: a person or system that decides which path people or things should take
senses.definitionCN: 决定人或物该走哪条路的人或系统
senses.example: The router of the parade chose a quieter street.
senses.exampleCN: 游行路线的安排人挑了一条更安静的街。
senses.why: The agent suffix -er gives the plain sense of one who routes, the human original of every machine that carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 表示「做这件事的人」，因此这个名字最早指的是为人指路的人，后来的机器都借用了这一身份。

senses.title: A tool that shapes a path in material
senses.definition: any tool that cuts or forms a channel for pipes, wires, or joints
senses.definitionCN: 在材料上为管道、电线或接缝开出通道的工具
senses.example: A wire router opened the channel along the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 一台开槽工具沿着墙开出了线槽。
senses.why: When a channel is cut into a surface, the tool has routed a path into the material, so the machine name spreads to any channel maker.
senses.whyCN: 当工具在材料表面切出通道时，就等于在材料里「铺了一条路」，于是这类开槽工具都能叫 router。

senses.title: A delivery route planner
senses.definition: a schedule or planner that sets the order in which stops are visited
senses.definitionCN: 规定各停靠点先后顺序的排程或规划程序
senses.example: The delivery router adds the new address to the round.
senses.exampleCN: 配送路线规划把新地址加进了这一趟行程。
senses.why: Naming an abstract plan a router shows the modern habit of treating route finding as a job done by a nameable thing.
senses.whyCN: 把抽象的安排称作 router，是现代英语把「找路」当成一件由某个可命名的事物来完成的习惯延伸。

senses.title: Figurative path finder
senses.definition: a person who finds a way forward for a group, especially in new territory
senses.definitionCN: 为群体找到前进道路的人，尤其在新领域中
senses.example: She became the router for the young research team.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了这支年轻研究团队的引路人。
senses.why: A figure of speech bends the physical path into a shared future, and someone who points the way for others gains this title.
senses.whyCN: 比喻把实体的路延伸到共同的未来，能为他人指出方向的人就被冠上这个称号。

intro.en: Router is formed in English from the Old French noun route and the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: router 是在英语内部由古法语名词 route（路线）加施事后缀 -er 构成的。

items.en: Rupta is the past participle of rumpere, to break, and names a broken way.
items.cn: rupta 是 rumpere（折断、打破）的过去分词，转指被开辟出来的路。

items.en: Route means a way or a march along a set path.
items.cn: 古法语 route 意为道路，或按既定路径行军。

items.en: Route enters English as a way or course of travel.
items.cn: route 进入英语，表示道路或行程。

items.en: Router first means a woodworking tool that cuts grooves, then a person who sets a route.
items.cn: router 先指在木料上开槽的工具，再指安排路线的人。

items.en: Engineers reuse the name for a device that routes network data.
items.cn: 工程师借用这个词来称呼为网络数据寻路的装置。

note.en: Router shares its base with route and routing, and is a neighbour of other network and cutting equipment.
note.cn: router 与 route、routing 同源，又与网络设备和切削工具相邻。

entries.definition: a way from one place to another
the choosing of a path for data or goods
to defeat completely and drive away
entries.definitionCN: 击溃；赶走。只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a device that turns signals into a form carried on a line
entries.definitionCN: 调制解调器；在电话线上转换信号的装置

entries.definition: a network device that passes frames between ports
entries.definitionCN: 交换机；在端口之间转发数据帧的网络设备

entries.definition: a person who shows the way to others

normalIntro.en: Router is route plus -er: a thing whose whole job is to give a route to what passes through.
normalIntro.cn: router 是 route 加 -er：一个把经过的东西都送上有路可走之处的存在。

normal.en: Route plus -er gives the doer of routing, so router is one who or which routes.
normal.cn: route 加 -er 得到做这件事的角色，所以 router 就是负责找路的那个。

normal.en: A wireless router spreads the signal through a flat without cables.
normal.cn: 无线路由器让住宅内不用网线也能有信号。

normal.en: To reset the router is the first cure for a dead home network.
normal.cn: 家里断网时，重启路由器往往是最有效的一招。

normal.en: The router forwards traffic, choosing the next hop for each packet.
normal.cn: 路由器负责转发流量，为每个数据包挑选下一站。

normal.en: Compare modem and router: the modem brings the line in, the router shares it out.
normal.cn: 对比 modem 与 router：前者把线路接进来，后者把线路分给各处。

abstract.en: Picture a junction post where every letter is handed a direction card.
abstract.cn: 想象路口有一座岗亭，每封信都会领到一张方向卡。

abstract.en: Imagine a carpenter drawing a thin groove across a plank.
abstract.cn: 想象木匠在木板上划出一条细槽。

abstract.en: Think of a guide leaning over a walker, pointing along the path.
abstract.cn: 想象向导俯身替行人指路。

examples.en: The router in the study keeps dropping the signal.
examples.cn: 书房里的路由器老是断信号。

examples.en: Set the router so that the printer shares the house network.
examples.cn: 设置一下路由器，让打印机接入家里的网络。

examples.en: A small guide router cut the channel for the new cable.
examples.cn: 小号开槽工具为新电线切出了线槽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「入特」——网络数据「入」网后各走其路，进哪条路由它特批；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rumpere（打破、折断）的过去分词 ruptus 转指被开辟的路 → 古法语 route（道路）→ 英语 route → route + -er = router（指路者；刨槽工具；路由器）。

sensesIntro.en: Router moves from a woodworking cutter to a network device, then widens to any path giver, physical or abstract.
sensesIntro.cn: router 从木工开槽工具走到网络转发装置，再扩展到各种铺路、指路的人与工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a junction post that points each message to its own road.
core.cn: 核心意象：路口岗亭把每条消息引向它该走的那条路。

branches.en: The network router is the everyday modern sense.
branches.cn: 网络路由器是今天最常用的义项。

branches.en: Both woodworking and channel tools cut a path into solid material.
branches.cn: 木工工具与开槽工具都是在实体材料里切出路来。

branches.en: The person who sets the route is the oldest sense of the suffix -er.
branches.cn: 安排路线的人是后缀 -er 最原始的指向。

branches.en: A delivery plan routes stops without any physical machine.
branches.cn: 配送规划在没有任何实体机器的情况下安排停靠顺序。

branches.en: A figurative router points people toward a future, as a guide does.
branches.cn: 比喻义中的引路者和向导一样，为人们指向未来。

intro.en: Router is built from the noun route and the agent suffix -er, with routing and routed growing beside it.
intro.cn: router 由名词 route 加施事后缀 -er 构成，旁边还长出了 routing 与 routed。

latinIntro.en: Behind route stands Latin rupt-, a broken opening that became a road.
latinIntro.cn: route 背后是拉丁语 rupt-，本指被破开的豁口，后来指道路。

items.example: Route is the base of router.
items.exampleCN: route 是 router 的基础词。

items.meaningCN: 做某事的人或物的后缀
items.example: The suffix -er turns route into router.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 route 变成 router。

items.meaning: a path setter or forwarding device
items.example: Router keeps the agent sense.
items.exampleCN: router 保留了施事含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms routing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 routing。

items.example: Routing names the work of a router.
items.exampleCN: routing 指路由器所做的工作。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms routed.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 routed。

items.example: Rupt- appears in rupture and interrupt.
items.exampleCN: rupt- 出现在 rupture 与 interrupt 中。

items.example: Ruptura helps explain the Old French form.
items.exampleCN: ruptura 有助解释古法语形式。

items.example: Rupture shares the same Latin root.
items.exampleCN: rupture 与它共享同一拉丁词根。

definition_zh: 王室成员；王位；王权；版税
definition_en: members of a royal family, or a payment for the right to use something
core_image: 王冠下的一排座位，再分出几枚金币流到作者手中
scene: 出版社按售出册数给作者结算版税。The publisher pays the author a royalty for every copy sold.
sceneCN: 这里 royalty 是「版税」（第 3 个义项：按使用量付给权利人的费用）；句意：出版社按售出册数给作者结算版税。

pos.zh: 王室；王族成员；王位；王权；版税

derivatives.zh: 王室的；皇家的；高贵的
以皇家规格地；极其
帝王般的；威严的（与 royal 同源于 rex 王）
弑君；弑君者（reg- 王 + 杀）

senses.title: The royal family as a class
senses.definition: the king and queen and their family, taken together as a body
senses.definitionCN: 国王、王后及其家人组成的整体
senses.example: The royalty of the small state attended the fair.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小国的王室成员出席了集市。
senses.why: Latin regalis means royal, and the noun royalty takes over the quality to name the whole group that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 regalis 意为王室的，名词 royalty 把这个性质变成了拥有它的整个人群。

senses.title: The title of a monarch
senses.definition: the rank, dignity, or sovereign power of a king or queen
senses.definitionCN: 国王或女王的身份、尊荣与最高权力
senses.example: He renounced his royalty to live in a village.
senses.exampleCN: 他放弃了王位，住进村庄。
senses.why: The abstract quality of being royal is also a legal status, so royalty comes to mean the dignity and power itself.
senses.whyCN: 「具有王室身份」这种抽象性质同时也是一种法定地位，于是 royalty 也能指那份尊荣与权力。

senses.title: A payment for the use of rights
senses.definition: a payment made to a creator or owner for the right to use, sell, or mine something
senses.definitionCN: 因使用、销售或开采某项资源而付给创作人或所有者的费用
senses.example: She earns a royalty on every book sold abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 每本海外售出的书她都能拿到一笔版税。
senses.why: A Crown that once claimed a share of the land and mines left behind the habit of paying a share for the right to use.
senses.whyCN: 历史上王室曾对土地与矿藏分走一部分收益，这种「因使用而分利」的做法保留下来，成为版税义。

senses.title: The natural resources claim of the Crown
senses.definition: the historical right of a sovereign to a share of gold, silver, or other minerals
senses.definitionCN: 君主历史上对金银等矿产享有的一份权利或分成
senses.example: Under old law, gold belonged to royal royalty.
senses.exampleCN: 依旧法，金银归属王室的矿产权。
senses.why: The fiscal side of royalty began with metals, which is why the word still names mineral and mining claims.
senses.whyCN: 版税这一财政意义肇始于金属矿产，所以这个词至今仍能指矿产与采矿方面的权利。

senses.title: A premium quality in manner
senses.definition: a manner or style that suggests kings and courtly dignity
senses.definitionCN: 举止或风格中透出的帝王气派与宫廷尊贵
senses.example: The old hall was treated with royalty by its stewards.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老厅堂被其管理员当作王宫来对待。
senses.why: The quality behind the noun keeps leaking into descriptions of how things are treated, so royalty can be a style as much as a rank.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词背后的「尊贵」性质不断渗入对事物待遇的描述，于是 royalty 既是等级，也是气派。

senses.title: A share paid for creative use
senses.definition: a fee paid each time a work, song, or design is performed or reproduced
senses.definitionCN: 作品、歌曲或设计每次被演出或复制时支付的费用
senses.example: Musicians collect a royalty when their songs are streamed.
senses.exampleCN: 歌曲被在线播放时，音乐人会收到演出版税。
senses.why: Modern media spreads the mining share to art, so every play or copy now carries a small payment, the clearest sense for the IELTS exam.
senses.whyCN: 现代媒体把矿产分成搬到艺术上，每一次播放或复制都带一小笔钱，这是雅思考试中最常见的意思。

intro.en: Royalty comes through Old French from Latin regalis, royal, built on rex, king.
intro.cn: royalty 经古法语来自拉丁语 regalis（王室的），其根是 rex（国王）。

items.en: Rex means king and regalis means belonging to a king.
items.cn: 拉丁语 rex 意为国王，regalis 意为属于国王的。

items.en: Regalitas names the quality of being kingly and royal privileges.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 regalitas 指王者的身份与王室特权。

items.en: Roialte carries the sense of royal rank and dignity.
items.cn: 古法语 roialte 保留王室等级与尊荣之意。

items.en: Royalty enters English as regal power and the royal people.
items.cn: royalty 进入英语，指王权与王室众人。

items.en: The Crown share of mines and later of printed books gives the money sense.
items.cn: 王室对矿藏、其后对印行书籍的分成，成就了「版税」这一义。

note.en: Royalty shares its root with royal and regal, and its money sense sits close to payment and fee words.
note.cn: royalty 与 royal、regal 同根，其版税义又与 payment、fee 等费用词相邻。

entries.definition: belonging to a king or queen
fit for a king, splendid
faithful to a person or cause
entries.definitionCN: 忠诚的；忠实的。只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 ligalis（合乎法律的）

entries.definition: a share of a sale paid to the person who makes it
entries.definitionCN: 促成交易者所得的回扣或佣金

entries.definition: money paid for a service or a right
a state ruled by a king or queen

normalIntro.en: Royalty is the noun of royal: first the people of the crown, then the privileges and money that came with the crown.
normalIntro.cn: royalty 是 royal 的名词形式：先指王冠下的人，再指与王冠相关的特权与钱款。

normal.en: Royal plus -ty gives the state of being royal, so royalty names royal people or royal status.
normal.cn: royal 加 -ty 表示「王室的状态」，所以 royalty 指王室成员或王室身份。

normal.en: Royalties are paid in the plural because each copy or play earns its own share.
normal.cn: 版税常用复数 royalties，因为每一册、每一次播放各自带来一份钱。

normal.en: A royalty rate is usually a percentage of the sale price.
normal.cn: 版税费率通常按售价的百分比计算。

normal.en: Compare royal and royalty: royal is what it is like, royalty is who or what it earns.
normal.cn: 对比 royal 与 royalty：前者说「像王室的」，后者说「是谁、赚了什么」。

normal.en: In patent law, a licensee pays a royalty to the inventor.
normal.cn: 在专利法里，被许可人向发明人支付专利使用费。

abstract.en: Picture a crown with a line of chairs under it, one for each family member.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠下排开一串座椅，每位家族成员都有一把。

abstract.en: Imagine a book that drips one coin into the writer hands per copy sold.
abstract.cn: 想象每卖出一本书，就有一枚硬币滴进作者手里。

abstract.en: Think of a small stream of coins from every play, page, and pint.
abstract.cn: 想象每次播放、每一页、每一瓶都引出细细一道金币。

examples.en: The singer receives a royalty each time the song is played.
examples.cn: 这首歌每播放一次，歌手就收到一笔版税。

examples.en: Members of royalty attended the opening ceremony.
examples.cn: 王室成员出席了开幕式。

examples.en: The company pays royalties to the designer for the pattern.
examples.cn: 公司为这一图样向设计师支付使用费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肉一贴」——版税就像把书卖出的钱「贴」给作者一块「肉」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rex（国王）→ regalis（王室的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 regalitas（王者身份、王室特权）→ 古法语 roialte → 英语 royalty，核心义「王室身份及其带来的特权与收益」。

sensesIntro.en: Royalty starts as the royal people and their status, then stretches to the privileges and payments attached to owning rights.
sensesIntro.cn: royalty 先从王室成员与身份出发，再延伸到与所有权相关的特权与分成款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crown, a row of seats beneath it, and a few coins flowing out to a creator.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶王冠、王冠下的一排座位，以及流向作者手中的几枚金币。

branches.en: The royal family as a body is the most familiar personal sense.
branches.cn: 把王室作为一个整体来称呼，是最常见的人身义项。

branches.en: Rank and courtly manner both name a quality of being royal.
branches.cn: 王位与宫廷气派都指向「具有王室性质」这一点。

branches.en: Payments for books, songs, or designs are the modern money sense.
branches.cn: 书籍、歌曲、设计的分成是现代的金钱义项。

branches.en: The Crown share of gold and silver is the historical source of the money sense.
branches.cn: 王室对金银的分成是金钱义项的历史源头。

branches.en: Mineral, publishing, and performance fees all pay a share for a right.
branches.cn: 矿产、出版与演出费用都是为某项权利支付一部分收益。

intro.en: Royalty is royal plus the noun suffix -ty, and the whole family gathers around Latin rex, king.
intro.cn: royalty 是 royal 加名词后缀 -ty，整族词都围绕拉丁语 rex（国王）。

latinIntro.en: Latin rex, king, gives regalis, royal, and through French the English word royalty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rex（国王）生出 regalis（王室的），再经法语变成英语 royalty。

items.example: Rex is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: rex 是整族词的根。

items.example: Regalis passes through French as royal.
items.exampleCN: regalis 经法语成为 royal。

items.example: Royal is the base of royalty.
items.exampleCN: royal 是 royalty 的基础词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ty forms royalty from royal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ty 把 royal 变成 royalty。

items.example: The suffix -al forms regalis from rex.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 由 rex 构成 regalis。

items.example: Regal keeps the Latin stem reg-.
items.exampleCN: regal 保留了拉丁词干 reg-。

items.example: Reign comes from Latin regnare, to rule.
items.exampleCN: reign 来自拉丁语 regnare（统治）。

items.example: Regicide joins king root to a killing root.
items.exampleCN: regicide 把表示国王的词根与表示杀戮的词根组合起来。

items.meaningCN: 空位期；两次在位之间的间歇
items.example: Interregnum means between kings.
items.exampleCN: interregnum 字面意思是「王与王之间」。

definition_zh: 基本的；初步的；简陋的；退化的
definition_en: basic and not developed, or left over from an earlier stage of evolution
core_image: 一块还没雕刻的粗糙木坯，上面只有最初的几道刻线
scene: 他只懂最基本的法语，在巴黎点菜都吃力。He only has a rudimentary knowledge of French and struggles to order in Paris.
sceneCN: 这里 rudimentary 是「基本的；初步的」（第 1 个义项：只具备最基础的程度）；句意：他只懂最基本的法语，在巴黎点菜都吃力。

pos.zh: 基本的；初步的；简陋的；退化的

derivatives.zh: 基本原理；初步知识；退化器官
基础知识；入门原理
以简陋或初步的方式
粗鲁；无礼（同源词 rude 的派生词，不经 rudimentary）

senses.title: At a basic level of knowledge or skill
senses.definition: existing only at the simplest basic level, not yet developed
senses.definitionCN: 只处在最简单的基础层面，尚未发展完善
senses.example: She has a rudimentary grasp of Spanish.
senses.exampleCN: 她对西班牙语只有初步的掌握。
senses.why: Latin rudimentum is the first try or the beginning of a thing, so anything rudimentary sits at the first step.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rudimentum 指最初的尝试或开端，因此 rudimentary 形容的事物都停在第一步。

senses.title: Simple to the point of being crude
senses.definition: made in a very simple or rough way, without refinement
senses.definitionCN: 以非常简单粗糙的方式做成的，未经精修
senses.example: The campers built a rudimentary shelter from sticks.
senses.exampleCN: 露营者用树枝搭了个简陋的住所。
senses.why: What is only begun is also unfinished, and an unfinished object looks crude beside a polished one.
senses.whyCN: 刚开头的东西也没完工，未完工的物件放在精致的成品旁边自然显得简陋。

senses.title: Left over in an undeveloped form
senses.definition: present in an organism or system only as an undeveloped remainder from an earlier stage
senses.definitionCN: 在生物体或系统中只作为早期阶段的未发育残留而存在
senses.example: The whale keeps rudimentary hind limbs inside its body.
senses.exampleCN: 鲸的身体内部留有退化的后肢。
senses.why: Biologists took the first beginnings of an organ and used rudimentary for parts that never grow, an early stage frozen in place.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借「器官的雏形」来形容永远不会长成的部分，即被定格的初期阶段。

senses.title: Barely adequate for a need
senses.definition: just enough to serve a purpose, with nothing to spare
senses.definitionCN: 刚够满足某个目的，毫无余裕
senses.example: A rudimentary breakfast was served at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时供应了勉强够吃的早餐。
senses.why: If a thing has only just begun to serve, it serves barely, so the word slips from beginnings to bare sufficiency.
senses.whyCN: 若一件事物才刚能派上用场，那也只是勉强够用，于是词义从「起点」滑向「仅够」。

senses.title: In need of much development
senses.definition: described as weak or unfinished when a stronger standard is expected
senses.definitionCN: 在应达到更高标准时被评价为薄弱或未完成
senses.example: The plan was rudimentary and full of gaps.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划还很粗糙，漏洞很多。
senses.why: Critics lean on the first-step sense to judge work that never got past its first step.
senses.whyCN: 评论者借用「第一步」之意，去评判那些始终没走出起点的作品。

senses.title: Of first principles in science or art
senses.definition: relating to the first principles or elements that a subject is built on
senses.definitionCN: 与某一学科赖以建立的最初原理或要素相关
senses.example: The course begins with rudimentary laws of motion.
senses.exampleCN: 课程从最基础的运动定律讲起。
senses.why: Latin rudiments are the first elements of any art, so this adjective can point to the earliest principles themselves.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rudimenta 指任何技艺的最初要素，因此这个词也能直接指最初的原理。

intro.en: Rudimentary comes from Latin rudimentum, a first attempt, through the related English noun rudiment.
intro.cn: rudimentary 来自拉丁语 rudimentum（最初的尝试），经由相关的英语名词 rudiment 进入英语。

items.en: The root rudi- is usually linked to rudis, rough or unworked.
items.cn: 词干 rudi- 一般认为与 rudis（粗糙的、未加工的）同源。

items.en: Rudimentum means a first attempt and the beginnings of a subject.
items.cn: rudimentum 意为初次尝试，也指一门学问的入门。

items.en: Modern Latin rudimentum is also used for an undeveloped organ.
items.cn: 近代拉丁语 rudimentum 也被用来指未发育的器官。

items.en: The noun rudiment and the adjective rudimentary join the language, first for basics and rough work.
items.cn: 名词 rudiment 与形容词 rudimentary 进入英语，初义为入门知识与粗制品。

items.en: Biology extends rudimentary to organs that never develop fully.
items.cn: 生物学把 rudimentary 扩展到始终未完全发育的器官。

note.en: Rudimentary grows from the noun rudiment and belongs beside rude, while its meaning field holds basic and primitive words.
note.cn: rudimentary 由名词 rudiment 派生，与 rude 同族；语义上又和表示基本、原始的词语相邻。

entries.definition: a first principle or an undeveloped part
entries.definitionCN: 基本原理；未发育的部分

entries.definition: in a rough or impolite manner
red and healthy looking
entries.definitionCN: 红润健康的。只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: simple and forming the starting point
belonging to the earliest stage
dealing with first simple principles

normalIntro.en: Rudimentary is rudiment plus -ary: whatever belongs to the first beginnings of a thing.
normalIntro.cn: rudimentary 是 rudiment 加 -ary：凡属于某事物最初开端的东西。

normal.en: Rudiment plus -ary gives the adjective of beginnings, so rudimentary means at the first stage.
normal.cn: rudiment 加 -ary 得到表示开端的形容词，所以 rudimentary 意为处在最初阶段。

normal.en: The rudiments of a subject are the first things you learn.
normal.cn: 一门学科的基础即是入门最先要学的东西。

normal.en: A rudimentary tool does its job badly but does it.
normal.cn: 简陋的工具干得不好，但总算干得成。

normal.en: Rudimentary knowledge is a start, not mastery.
normal.cn: 基础知识只是起点，并非精通。

normal.en: Compare rudimentary and basic: basic is neutral, rudimentary hints at crudeness.
normal.cn: 对比 rudimentary 与 basic：basic 中性，rudimentary 暗含粗糙未成。

abstract.en: Picture a wood block with only the first guide lines cut into it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木坯，上面只划了几条最初的定位线。

abstract.en: Imagine a camp shelter of three bent branches and a few leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象用三根弯树枝和几片叶子搭成的营地住所。

abstract.en: Think of a faint stub inside a drawing of a whale, a leg that never grew.
abstract.cn: 想象鲸的解剖图里有一小截淡色的残迹，那是一条从未长成的腿。

examples.en: His knowledge of the rules was rudimentary at best.
examples.cn: 他对规则的了解充其量只是皮毛。

examples.en: The village school offers a rudimentary education.
examples.cn: 这所村校提供的是初步的教育。

examples.en: The drawing is still rudimentary, but it gives clear direction.
examples.cn: 这张图仍然粗糙，却给出了明确的方向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「入地门」——刚「入地门」的新手只会最基本的招；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rudis（粗糙的、未加工的）→ rudimentum（最初的尝试、入门原理）→ 英语 rudiment → rudimentary（基本的；简陋的；退化残留的），核心义「尚在最初阶段」。

sensesIntro.en: Rudimentary begins with first-step knowledge, moves to crude and barely sufficient things, and ends with undeveloped leftovers and first principles.
sensesIntro.cn: rudimentary 从「第一步的知识」出发，过渡到简陋与勉强够用，最后落到未发育的残留与最初原理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough wooden block with only the first few guide lines on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块粗糙木坯，上面只有最初几条定位线。

branches.en: Basic knowledge and first principles are the beginnings of a subject.
branches.cn: 基础知识与原理都是学科的开端。

branches.en: Crude work and unfinished plans are the same thing judged from different sides.
branches.cn: 粗糙的作品与未完成的计划是同一件事从两个角度看。

branches.en: An undeveloped organ is a first stage frozen in place.
branches.cn: 未发育的器官是被定格的初期阶段。

branches.en: Barely sufficient means the work has only just begun to serve.
branches.cn: 勉强够用意味着它才刚开始能派上用场。

branches.en: A learner with only the basics also has only just enough to get by.
branches.cn: 只掌握基础的学习者也正好只够应付。

intro.en: Rudimentary is rudiment plus the adjective suffix -ary, with rudiment and rudiments beneath it and rude beside it.
intro.cn: rudimentary 是 rudiment 加形容词后缀 -ary，下面有 rudiment 与 rudiments，旁边还有同源的 rude。

latinIntro.en: Latin rudis, rough and unworked, gives rudimentum, a first attempt, and then English rudimentary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rudis（粗糙、未加工）生出 rudimentum（最初的尝试），再到英语 rudimentary。

items.example: Rudis supplies the rough image behind the word.
items.exampleCN: rudis 提供了这个词背后的粗糙意象。

items.example: Rudimentum is the direct source of rudiment.
items.exampleCN: rudimentum 是 rudiment 的直接来源。

items.example: Rudiment keeps the beginning sense.
items.exampleCN: rudiment 保留了开端之意。

items.meaning: the first elements of a subject
items.example: The plural names the basics of a subject.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式指一门学问的基础。

items.meaning: a thing resulting from an action
items.example: The suffix -ment forms rudimentum.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 rudimentum。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms rudimentary from rudiment.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 把 rudiment 变成 rudimentary。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms rudimentarily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 rudimentarily。

items.example: Rude descends from the same Latin rudis.
items.exampleCN: rude 同出拉丁语 rudis。

items.example: Rudeness is formed from rude.
items.exampleCN: rudeness 由 rude 构成。

items.meaning: a tool for rubbing out marks
items.example: Eraser shares Latin radere, to scrape, with rudis.
items.exampleCN: eraser 与 rudis 共享拉丁语 radere（刮擦）。

definition_zh: 隆隆声；低沉的轰响；发出隆隆声；隆隆作响地滚动；街头斗殴
definition_en: a low continuous heavy sound, or to make such a sound while moving or shaking
core_image: 远处载重卡车驶过，地面跟着低沉地震动
scene: 深夜的雷声还没停，屋顶上就传来了低沉的隆隆声。At midnight, a low rumble rolled across the hills and shook the windows.
sceneCN: 这里 rumble 是「隆隆声」（第 1 个义项：低沉而持续的巨大声响）；句意：午夜时分，低沉的隆隆声滚过山丘，震得窗户发颤。

pos.zh: 发出隆隆声；隆隆作响地行进
用低沉的声音说；使发出隆隆声

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成的动名词，义为「隆隆声；持续的抱怨声」
动词加 -er 构成的施事名词，义为「发出隆隆声的东西」
动词加 -y 构成的形容词，义为「发出隆隆低响的」
形容词再加 -ly，义为「伴随着隆隆声地」

senses.title: A low heavy continuous sound
senses.definition: a deep, heavy, fairly long sound, like thunder or a big engine
senses.definitionCN: 低沉、厚重而持续较久的声响，如雷声或大型发动机的声音
senses.example: We heard the rumble of thunder far away.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见远处雷声隆隆。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is imitative: the mouth makes a rolled consonant sound that copies a heavy rolling noise.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层是拟声：口腔滚动的辅音在模仿沉重滚动的声音，所以核心意象就是「沉沉震响」。

senses.title: To make a heavy rolling sound
senses.definition: to make a long deep sound that rolls and shakes, as thunder or a lorry does
senses.definitionCN: 像雷或重型卡车那样发出绵长而震动的低沉声响
senses.example: Thunder rumbled over the valley for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 雷声在山谷上空滚了好几个小时。
senses.why: If the noise exists, something is producing it, so the noun naturally turns into a verb of sounding.
senses.whyCN: 既然声音存在，就必有东西在发声，于是名词自然转化为表示「发响」的动词。

senses.title: To move with a rumbling sound
senses.definition: to move along slowly and heavily while making a deep sound
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢沉重地行进，同时发出低沉的声响
senses.example: A coal train rumbled past the old station.
senses.exampleCN: 一列运煤火车隆隆地驶过旧车站。
senses.why: Heavy wheels on rails and tyres on rough ground disturb the air and the earth, so motion and the rumbling sound travel together.
senses.whyCN: 重轮碾过铁轨、轮胎压过粗地面时会扰动空气与地面，所以「移动」和「隆隆声」总是同时到来。

senses.title: A growling stomach
senses.definition: a low gurgling sound that the stomach makes when a person is hungry
senses.definitionCN: 饥饿时腹中发出的低沉咕咕声
senses.example: Everyone laughed when his stomach gave a loud rumble.
senses.exampleCN: 他的肚子大声咕咕一叫，大家都笑了。
senses.why: The body borrows the word for any deep inner noise, and the stomach is the place everyone hears such a noise.
senses.whyCN: 身体借用了这个词来形容一切深沉的内部响声，而肚子正是人人都会听到这种响声的地方。

senses.title: A shout of disapproval
senses.definition: a low sound made by a group of people to show that they do not agree with someone
senses.definitionCN: 一群人低沉着发声音，表示对某人的不满或反对
senses.example: A rumble of protest rose from the back of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅后方响起一阵低沉的抗议声。
senses.why: A crowd does not vote; it growls, so its disagreement becomes an audible rumble in the room.
senses.whyCN: 人群不是投票，而是低吼，于是他们的不满在房间里变成一片听得见的低沉声响。

senses.title: A grumbling speech
senses.definition: to say something slowly and quietly in a low, rough voice
senses.definitionCN: 以缓慢、低沉而粗哑的嗓音说话
senses.example: He rumbled a few words of thanks before leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 他低沉着嗓音道了声谢，然后离开了。
senses.why: A voice deep enough to feel in the chest sounds like distant thunder, so it earns the same word.
senses.whyCN: 低到能在胸腔里感受到的嗓音，听起来就像远处的雷，因此借用了同一个词。

senses.title: A continuing argument
senses.definition: used with on: to continue for a long time, usually of an argument or complaint
senses.definitionCN: 常与 on 连用，指争论或抱怨长期持续不停
senses.example: The dispute over the new road still rumbles on.
senses.exampleCN: 围绕新公路的争论仍在持续发酵。
senses.why: Thunder that will not stop becomes a metaphor for quarrels that refuse to fade, so the sound of the sky names a stubborn dispute.
senses.whyCN: 停不下来的雷声被比作不肯平息的争吵，于是天空的声响用来指一场顽固的争执。

senses.title: A street fight
senses.definition: a fight between two groups, usually of young people in a public street
senses.definitionCN: 两伙人的冲突，通常指年轻人在公共街道上的群殴
senses.example: Police were called after a rumble broke out outside the club.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部外爆发街头斗殴后，警方被叫来。
senses.why: The sound sense then names an event that is loud through and through, so a brawling crowd becomes a rumble.
senses.whyCN: 声响义项进一步用来指整个事件，因为这种事件从头到尾都很嘈杂，于是打架的人群本身就叫作一场喧嚣。

intro.en: Rumble is probably an imitative word of the Middle English period, built on the rolling r sound, with the frequentative -le ending, and its deep noise sense has never left it.
intro.cn: rumble 很可能是中古英语时期形成的拟声词，以滚动的 r 音为骨架，加上表示反复动作的 -le 后缀，「低沉轰鸣」这一核心义从未离开过它。

items.en: A rolled r plus a dull m suggests a heavy noise that keeps going; the exact origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 滚动的 r 音加上沉闷的 m 暗示持续不停的重响；确切来源不确定。

items.en: Forms such as romble and rumble appear, and the word means to sound with a low heavy noise.
items.cn: 出现 romble、rumble 这类拼写，词义为低沉厚重地发响。

items.en: The -le ending, common in words of repeated small action, fixes the idea of a continuous rolling sound.
items.cn: 表示反复动作的 -le 词尾十分常见，它把「持续滚动的声响」固定了下来。

items.en: The noun is regular beside the verb, naming thunder, engines, and passing vehicles.
items.cn: 名词与动词并行使用，指雷、发动机与驶过的车辆。

items.en: Slang adds the street fight sense, and the phrase with on adds the sense of a dispute that goes on.
items.cn: 俚语增添了街头斗殴义，与 on 连用的短语则增添了争执持续不息的义项。

items.en: The word is used for inner noises too, such as a hungry stomach or a growing crowd.
items.cn: 现代英语也用它指内部声响，比如饥饿的肚子或渐渐骚动的人群。

note.en: Rumble sits with echoic rolling sounds such as rumbling and rumbly, and with nearby noise words such as grumble and thunder.
note.cn: rumble 与 rumbling、rumbly 等同属表示滚动声响的拟声词族，也与 grumble、thunder 等「声响」类词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Rumble is a rolled r plus a -le ending, so the mouth itself shows a heavy sound that keeps going.
normalIntro.cn: rumble 由滚动的 r 音加 -le 词尾构成，嘴巴发音时就已经在演示「持续不停的重响」。

normal.en: The rumble of thunder comes from the sky.
normal.cn: rumble of thunder 就是天上的隆隆雷声。

normal.en: A lorry rumbles down the street on heavy wheels.
normal.cn: 大卡车用沉重的轮子隆隆地驶过街道。

normal.en: A hungry stomach gives a low rumble before lunch.
normal.cn: 午饭前饿着的肚子会发出低低的咕咕声。

normal.en: If a dispute rumbles on, it refuses to end.
normal.cn: 争论 rumble on，就是一直不肯结束。

normal.en: Compare grumble: grumble is complaining, rumble is the deep sound itself.
normal.cn: 对比 grumble：grumble 是低声抱怨，rumble 只是那种深沉的响声本身。

abstract.en: Picture thunder rolling across the far horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象雷声沿远处的地平线一路滚过。

abstract.en: Hear the deep vibration in your chest when a truck passes.
abstract.cn: 感受卡车驶过时胸腔里那种深沉的震动。

abstract.en: See a heavy wheel turning slowly and shaking the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的轮子缓缓转动，把地面震得发抖。

examples.en: A low rumble of thunder warned them that the storm was near.
examples.cn: 一阵低沉的雷声提醒他们暴风雨已经不远了。

examples.en: The trucks rumbled through the narrow street all night.
examples.cn: 卡车整夜隆隆地穿过狭窄的街道。

examples.en: Leaders met again as the argument over the budget rumbled on.
examples.cn: 预算之争仍在持续发酵，领导人再次会面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「让布儿」——布匹拖过地面会发出低沉的响动，联想隆隆声；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为出自中古英语的拟声词形（romble、rumble），以滚动的 r 音模拟沉重轰鸣，并受 -le 反复后缀的影响；词根真正的拟声来源不确定。由「低沉持续的响声」引申出鸣响、隆隆地移动、肚子咕咕叫等义项，再由嘈杂的群体场景引申出街头斗殴与争执持续之意。

sensesIntro.en: Rumble starts as the deep sound of thunder or engines, becomes the act of making that sound, then spreads to moving bodies, voices, crowds, and finally to a loud brawl.
sensesIntro.cn: rumble 先是雷或发动机的低沉巨响，接着指发出这种声响的动作，再扩展到移动的物体、嗓音、人群，最后泛指喧嚣的群殴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy lorry rolling past and shaking the windows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆重型卡车隆隆驶过，震得窗户发颤。

branches.en: The deep continuous noise is the basic noun sense.
branches.cn: 低沉持续的巨响是最基本的名词义。

branches.en: Making the sound is the basic verb sense.
branches.cn: 发出这种声响是最基本的动词义。

branches.en: A rolling train and a growling stomach both fill the body with low vibration.
branches.cn: 隆隆驶过的火车与咕咕作响的肚子，都会让身体充满低沉震动。

branches.en: A crowd and a speaker can both produce deep low sound.
branches.cn: 人群与说话者都能发出低沉厚重的声音。

branches.en: Sound that will not stop becomes a dispute or a brawl.
branches.cn: 停不下来的声响演化成争执或群殴。

intro.en: Rumble is a root imitative word rather than a word built from prefixes, so its pieces are the rolled r sound and the -le ending that marks repeated action.
intro.cn: rumble 是词根性的拟声词，并非由前缀拼成，可供拆解的是滚动的 r 音与表示反复动作的 -le 词尾。

latinIntro.en: Rumble has no reliable Latin cognate, so the related forms here are the English word family with imitative and frequentative pieces.
latinIntro.cn: rumble 没有可靠的拉丁语同源词，因此这里列出的是由拟声成分与反复后缀构成的英语词族。

items.meaningCN: 滚动、沉重而低沉的声响
items.example: The r and m imitate a heavy noise.
items.exampleCN: r 与 m 的组合模仿沉重的响声。

items.example: The -le ending makes the noise keep going.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -le 让声响持续不断。

items.meaning: forming a noun from a verb
items.example: The suffix -ing forms rumbling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 rumbling。

items.example: The suffix -y forms rumbly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 rumbly。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms rumbler.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 rumbler。

items.example: The particle on gives rumbles on.
items.exampleCN: 小品词 on 构成 rumbles on。
