items.example: Grumble looks close but has its own history.
items.exampleCN: grumble 看着相近，但有自己的来历。

items.example: Fumble shares only the sound shape.
items.exampleCN: fumble 只与它共享语音外形。

items.example: Tumble also ends in the -le sound.
items.exampleCN: tumble 同样以 -le 音结尾。

definition_zh: 无情的；残忍的；冷酷无情的；不择手段的
definition_en: showing no pity for other people and ready to hurt them to get what you want
core_image: 一个人踩过倒下的对手继续向前，头也不回
scene: 为了抢下那笔订单，公司毫不留情地砍掉了整条团队，连老员工也没有例外。In its fight for the contract, the company was ruthless with anyone who stood in the way.
sceneCN: 这里 ruthless 是「无情的」（第 1 个义项：对他人毫无怜悯、肯为达目的造成伤害）；句意：争夺那份合同时，公司对任何挡路的人都毫不留情。

pos.zh: 无情的；残忍的；冷酷的、毫无怜悯的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「无情地；毫不留情地」
形容词加 -ness 构成的抽象名词，义为「无情；残忍」
构成 ruthless 的词基，义为「怜悯；同情」，现多用于否定语境
词基加 -ful 构成的形容词，义为「充满怜悯的」，现已罕用

senses.title: Showing no pity
senses.definition: willing to hurt or use other people with no feeling of pity
senses.definitionCN: 肯伤害或利用他人而毫无怜悯之心
senses.example: The ruthless ruler jailed anyone who opposed him.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冷酷的统治者把反对他的人都关进监狱。
senses.why: The word is a cancelled pity: -less denies ruth, the old English word for compassion, so ruthless describes a heart with no mercy left in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是把「怜悯」取消掉：-less 否定了古英语中表示同情的词基 ruth，所以 ruthless 描述的是心里再也留不下一丝慈悲。

senses.title: Hard in business or sport
senses.definition: very hard and determined, willing to use harsh methods in business, politics, or sport
senses.definitionCN: 极其强硬果决，在生意、政治或体育中肯使用严厉手段
senses.example: A ruthless competitor will undercut every rival.
senses.exampleCN: 不择手段的竞争者会把每个对手的价格都压低。
senses.why: Business and sport reward whoever reaches the goal first, so the missing pity becomes a tool chosen for conditions like these.
senses.whyCN: 生意场和赛场奖励的是先到达目标的人，于是「怜悯缺失」在这里变成一件被选用的工具。

senses.title: Harsh and severe
senses.definition: very severe and sudden, leaving no room for comfort or delay
senses.definitionCN: 非常严厉而突然，不留任何缓冲余地
senses.example: The company carried out ruthless cost cuts last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 公司去年冬天进行了严酷的成本削减。
senses.why: A measure can be ruthless when it is applied without a pause for those it hurts, so the vanished mercy attaches to actions rather than to people.
senses.whyCN: 当一项措施不顾受牵连者、连停顿都没有地推行时，它就成了严酷的；于是消失的仁慈从人身上转移到了做法上。

senses.title: Serving the purpose only
senses.definition: chosen only because it works, without any care for fairness or kindness
senses.definitionCN: 只为奏效而选择，全然不顾公平与善意
senses.example: Their ruthless logic left no space for human weakness.
senses.exampleCN: 他们冷酷的逻辑没有给人之常情留任何空间。
senses.why: When only results are weighed, the absence of mercy stops looking like cruelty and starts looking like efficiency.
senses.whyCN: 当只衡量结果时，缺失的怜悯就不再像残忍，而开始像是效率。

senses.title: Spoken of in praise of toughness
senses.titleCN: （褒义地）一往无前、毫不手软的
senses.definition: sometimes approving, describing someone who never lets feelings weaken their effort
senses.definitionCN: 有时用作褒义，形容人不让情感削弱自己的行动
senses.example: She was ruthless in cutting things she could not finish.
senses.exampleCN: 她毫不手软地砍掉了自己完成不了的事。
senses.why: The same missing pity under the sign of praise becomes resolve, because a person who cuts without regret often finishes what others drop.
senses.whyCN: 同一种缺失的怜悯被放进称赞的语感里，就变成了果决，因为毫不心软的人往往能完成别人放弃的事。

intro.en: Ruthless is the adjective -less added to ruth, an old English noun for pity; ruth survives today only in this negative shape and in the opposite ruthless, so the word means pity-without.
intro.cn: ruthless 是形容词后缀 -less 加在古英语名词 ruth（怜悯）之后构成的；ruth 今天几乎只在这类否定形式里留存，所以这个词的字面意思就是「没有怜悯」。

items.en: The noun ruth means sorrow or compassion, related to the verb rue, to feel regret.
items.cn: 名词 ruth 意为悲伤或同情，与表示悔恨的动词 rue 同源。

items.en: The suffix -leas marks a lack, as in the modern -less forms.
items.cn: 后缀 -leas 表示缺少，相当于现代英语的 -less。

items.en: Rutheles, the older spelling, already names a person without mercy.
items.cn: 较早的拼写 rutheles 已经用来指毫无怜悯之心的人。

items.en: Ruth itself fades into literary and negative use, while ruthless grows common.
items.cn: ruth 本身退入书面与否定用法，ruthless 却日渐常用。

items.en: The word moves into business and sport, where being ruthless can even be praised.
items.cn: 这个词进入商业与体育语境，此时「无情」甚至可以是一种称赞。

items.en: Through the adverb and the noun is the word applied to whole company cultures.
items.cn: 经由派生副词与名词，这个词被用来形容整个企业文化。

note.en: Ruthless belongs to the ruth family with ruth and ruthlessly, and to a compact set of words about hardness of heart, from cruel to brutal.
note.cn: ruthless 与 ruth、ruthlessly 同属一个词族，并与 cruel、brutal 等表达「心硬」的词构成一个紧凑的词义场。

entries.definition: the quality of having no pity
pity or sorrow for others
to feel regret about something
willing to cause pain to others
very violent or extremely harsh
showing no kindness at all
entries.definitionCN: 毫不仁慈的；无怜悯心的

normalIntro.en: Ruthless is ruth, old English for pity, plus -less, so the word can be read as mercy missing.
normalIntro.cn: ruthless 就是古英语表示怜悯的 ruth 加上「没有」的后缀 -less，因此可以读成「少了怜悯」。

normal.en: Strip ruth and add -less: no pity is left.
normal.cn: 去掉 ruth 加上 -less：一点怜悯都不剩。

normal.en: A ruthless dictator rules by fear and silence.
normal.cn: 无情的独裁者靠恐惧与沉默来统治。

normal.en: Ruthless competition cares only about winning.
normal.cn: 无情的竞争只在乎赢。

normal.en: The adverb ruthlessly ends in -ly, as all adverbs do.
normal.cn: 副词 ruthlessly 和其他副词一样以 -ly 结尾。

normal.en: Compare merciless: both mean no pity, but ruthless keeps the old root of compassion.
normal.cn: 对比 merciless：两者都表示毫无怜悯，但 ruthless 保留了那个古老词根「慈悲」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that closes before the word please is heard.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌在听到「请」字之前就已经关上。

abstract.en: Think of a chess player who never hesitates over a lost pawn.
abstract.cn: 想象一位棋手从不为一枚失去的兵犹豫。

abstract.en: See a blade that never asks whether the target deserves it.
abstract.cn: 想象一柄从不关心目标是否应得的刀刃。

examples.en: The ruthless manager fired half the team without a word of warning.
examples.cn: 那位无情的经理一声招呼都不打就解雇了半个团队。

examples.en: She is ruthless when it comes to meeting deadlines.
examples.cn: 一到赶截止日期时，她毫不留情。

examples.en: Ruthlessness was widely reported as the company culture.
examples.cn: 无情被广泛报道为那家公司的文化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ruless」——心里没有「情面」这条规则，便成了无情；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ruth（悲伤；怜悯，与动词 rue「懊悔」同源）+ 表示「缺少」的后缀 -less → ruthless，字面义「没有怜悯」→ 无情、残忍；17 世纪后 ruth 本身几近消失，ruthless 反而成为常用词，并扩展出「生意中不择手段」「措施严厉」等用法。

sensesIntro.en: Ruthless begins with a heart that has no pity, then widens to hard competitors, severe measures, methods chosen only for results, and finally to a kind of praised single-mindedness.
sensesIntro.cn: ruthless 从「心里没有怜悯」出发，随后扩展到强硬的竞争者、严厉的措施、只求奏效的手段，最后甚至成为一种被称赞的专注。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone stepping over a fallen rival without looking back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人跨过倒下的对手继续往前走，连头都不回。

branches.en: A heart with no pity is the basic sense of the word.
branches.cn: 没有怜悯的心是这个词的基本义。

branches.en: Fighting for a place turns the missing pity into a business tactic.
branches.cn: 争夺位置把缺失的怜悯变成了商业手段。

branches.en: Severity is ruthlessness applied to measures rather than people.
branches.cn: 严厉是把无情施加在措施而不是人身上。

branches.en: Logic that ignores feelings is the same missing pity described as habit.
branches.cn: 不顾感受的逻辑，就是同一种缺失的怜悯被描述成习惯。

branches.en: The same hardness can help a rival in a deal or help a person push through a hard task.
branches.cn: 同一种硬气既能用来在交易中击败对手，也能帮人硬撑过艰难任务。

intro.en: Ruthless is a clean two-piece word: an old English noun for pity and the suffix that takes it away.
intro.cn: ruthless 是一个结构清楚的两段式词：一个古英语中表示怜悯的名词，加上把这份怜悯拿走的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Ruthless has no Latin relative, so this list shows the English pieces and the word family built on them.
latinIntro.cn: ruthless 没有拉丁语同族词，因此这里列出的只是它的英语构件与由这些构件构成的词族。

items.meaningCN: 怜悯；为他人感到的悲伤
items.example: Ruth is the old noun inside ruthless.
items.exampleCN: ruth 是 ruthless 内部那个古老的名词。

items.example: The suffix -less turns ruth into ruthless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 把 ruth 变成 ruthless。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms ruthlessly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 ruthlessly。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms ruthlessness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 ruthlessness。

items.example: The suffix -ful could contrast ruthless with a full of pity form.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 可以构成与 ruthless 相对的「充满怜悯」形式。

items.example: The old suffix -leas became modern -less.
items.exampleCN: 古老后缀 -leas 演变为今天的 -less。

items.example: Rue is the verb cousin of ruth.
items.exampleCN: rue 是 ruth 的动词近亲。

items.example: Merciless builds the same idea on a different root.
items.exampleCN: merciless 用另一个词根表达同样的意思。

items.meaning: a broad family of negative adjectives
items.meaningCN: 由该后缀构成的否定形容词汇族
items.example: Careless, helpless, and hopeless follow the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: careless、helpless、hopeless 都遵循同样的构词模式。

definition_zh: 黑麦；黑麦粒；黑麦面包；（美式用语）加了黑麦的美国威士忌
definition_en: a hardy cereal plant grown for its grain, or the flour bread and spirit made from that grain
core_image: 寒风里的田地上，一束细长的黑麦穗随风摇晃
scene: 北欧的冬天太冷，小麦常常冻死，农民于是改种更耐寒的黑麦，用它磨粉烤出深色的面包。Rye grows where wheat would fail, and its dark flour makes heavy bread.
sceneCN: 这里 rye 是「黑麦」（第 1 个义项：一种耐寒的禾谷类作物）；句意：黑麦长在小麦长不好的地方，它那深色的面粉能烤出扎实的面包。

pos.zh: 黑麦（植物）；黑麦粒；黑麦粉；黑麦面包；黑麦威士忌

derivatives.zh: 黑麦加 bread 构成的复合名词，义为「黑麦面包」
黑麦加 grass 构成的复合名词，指黑麦草，与谷物黑麦不同
黑麦加 whisky 构成的复合名词，指以黑麦为主的威士忌

senses.title: The cereal plant
senses.definition: a hardy cereal plant grown in cool or poor soils for its grain
senses.definitionCN: 一种耐寒的禾谷类作物，可在寒冷或贫瘠的土壤中种植以取其谷粒
senses.example: Farmers in the far north grow rye on thin soils.
senses.exampleCN: 极北地区的农民在贫瘠的土地上种植黑麦。
senses.why: The oldest English word for the grain names the plant first, because a crop is known by the stalk in the field before its products are named.
senses.whyCN: 这个英语词最初指的就是这种谷物的植株，因为作物总是先在田里以茎叶的形态被人认识，然后才有由它制成的产品名称。

senses.title: The grain as foodstuff
senses.definition: the grain of this plant, or the flour made from it, used for bread and other food
senses.definitionCN: 这种植物的谷粒，或由其磨成的面粉，用于面包及其他食品
senses.example: She mixed rye with wheat flour for the loaf.
senses.exampleCN: 她用黑麦粉和小麦粉混合做那条面包。
senses.why: Once the grain is harvested and milled, the same word smoothly names the food material rather than the standing plant.
senses.whyCN: 谷粒一旦收割并磨成粉，同一个词便顺理成章地指向食材，而不再是立在田里的植株。

senses.title: Rye bread
senses.definition: bread made from rye flour, usually dark and dense with a sour flavour
senses.definitionCN: 用黑麦粉做的面包，通常颜色深、质地紧实并带酸味
senses.example: A slice of rye goes well with strong cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 一片黑麦面包配味浓的奶酪很合适。
senses.why: Bread is named after its flour by a simple transfer, and the dark sour loaf becomes so typical that it takes the short name of the grain.
senses.whyCN: 面包由所用的粉得名，这种深色微酸的面包又太有代表性，于是直接占用了谷物的短名。

senses.title: Rye whisky
senses.definition: an American or Canadian whisky distilled mainly from rye grain
senses.definitionCN: 主要用黑麦谷粒酿造的美国或加拿大威士忌
senses.example: He ordered a rye on the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯加冰的黑麦威士忌。
senses.why: Distillers name a drink after its main grain, so the short word for the grain becomes the short word for the glass poured at a bar.
senses.whyCN: 酿酒者用主要谷物给酒命名，于是谷物的短名又成了酒吧里推过来的那杯酒的短名。

senses.title: A field of rye
senses.definition: the plant seen as a whole crop filling a field
senses.definitionCN: 把这种植物看作大片铺满田地的作物
senses.example: The children ran through the tall rye.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在高高的黑麦田里奔跑。
senses.why: When many stalks stand together they read as landscape, so the grain name drifts naturally to a place and not just a plant.
senses.whyCN: 当成千上万根茎秆连成一片时，人看到的就是风景，所以谷物的名字自然漂移到「地点」而不是「植物」上。

intro.en: Rye matches the same grain name across the Germanic languages, so it is best understood as a Germanic word, not a Latin one.
intro.cn: rye 与日耳曼各语言中的「黑麦」名称一一对应，因此语言学家是重构出一个共同的日耳曼语形式，而不是从拉丁语沿袭而来。

items.en: A word generally reconstructed as rugiz or raig meant the rye grain across the Germanic area.
items.cn: 一般认为在日耳曼语区域内存在一个重构形式 rugiz 或 raig，指黑麦谷粒。

items.en: The plant already has names such as ryge, spelling the Germanic consonant with a y sound.
items.cn: 这个植物在古英语中已有 ryge 之类的名称，用 y 表示日耳曼语的辅音。

items.en: The Norse form rugr supports the same Germanic root.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语的 rugr 形式支持这同一个日耳曼词根。

items.en: The spelling settles as rye, and the word spreads from plant to grain to bread.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 rye，词义也从植株扩展到谷粒与面包。

items.en: Baking and distilling make rye bread and rye whisky common everyday terms.
items.cn: 烘焙与酿酒让黑麦面包和黑麦威士忌成为日常用语。

items.en: Rye appears in titles and songs, so a crop name becomes a literary image.
items.cn: 黑麦出现在书名与歌曲里，一个作物名于是成了文学意象。

note.en: Rye is close in spelling and sound to ryegrass and to other grain names such as barley, wheat, and oats, all of which belong to the same field of meaning.
note.cn: rye 在拼写与读音上与 ryegrass 相近，并与其他谷物名 barley、wheat、oats 同属「谷物」词义场。

entries.definition: a quick growing grass used for pasture
entries.definitionCN: 黑麦草，一种用于牧草的快生禾草，名字含 rye 但并非真正的黑麦

entries.definition: bread made from rye flour
twisted, or showing dry humour
entries.definitionCN: 歪斜的；带着冷嘲的，只是读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a cereal grown for grain and malt
a cereal that gives flour for white bread
a cereal grain used for porridge

normalIntro.en: Rye keeps the same grain shape across the Germanic languages and appears in a few everyday compounds that are worth learning together.
normalIntro.cn: rye 在日耳曼各语言里保持着同样的谷物含义，并出现在几个值得一起记住的日常复合词中。

normal.en: Rye bread is dark, dense, and slightly sour.
normal.cn: rye bread 颜色深、质地紧、略带酸味。

normal.en: Rye flour is what makes the loaf dark.
normal.cn: rye flour 就是让面包发深色的黑麦粉。

normal.en: Rye whisky is distilled mainly from rye grain.
normal.cn: rye whisky 主要用黑麦谷粒酿造。

normal.en: Ryegrass is a pasture grass, not the grain itself.
normal.cn: ryegrass 是牧草，并不是那种谷物本身。

normal.en: Compare wheat: wheat needs better soil, rye survives in the cold.
normal.cn: 对比 wheat：小麦需要更好的土壤，黑麦则能在寒冷中活下来。

abstract.en: Picture thin stalks bending together in an icy wind.
abstract.cn: 想象细长的麦秆在寒风中一起弯下去。

abstract.en: See a dark heavy loaf sliced on a wooden board.
abstract.cn: 想象木板上切开的一条深色厚实面包。

abstract.en: Hear the same short sound rye echoing across northern farmlands.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个短促的读音 rye 在北方农田之间回荡。

examples.en: Farmers in cold regions plant rye because it survives the frost.
examples.cn: 寒冷地区的农民种植黑麦，因为它能耐霜冻。

examples.en: She prefers rye bread to white bread.
examples.cn: 她更喜欢黑麦面包而不是白面包。

examples.en: The recipe asks for two cups of rye flour.
examples.cn: 这个食谱需要两杯黑麦粉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来」——田野上「来」了一束黑麦；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自日耳曼语共同形式（重构作 rugiz 或 raig「黑麦」）→ 古英语 ryge → 中古英语 rye，与古诺尔斯语 rugr、德语 Roggen 同源；词根可靠，更早的印欧来源存疑。由「黑麦植株」扩展为谷粒、面粉，再借代出黑麦面包与黑麦威士忌。

sensesIntro.en: Rye names a tough cereal first, then its grain and flour, then the bread and the whisky that the grain makes, and finally the crop as a whole field.
sensesIntro.cn: rye 先指一种耐寒的禾谷，其次指它的谷粒与面粉，再指用谷粒做成的面包与威士忌，最后还能指整片田里的作物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bundle of thin rye stalks swaying in a cold wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束细长的黑麦穗在寒风里摇摆。

branches.en: The plant itself is the oldest and most basic sense.
branches.cn: 植株本身是最古老、最基本的义项。

branches.en: Harvesting turns the plant into grain and flour.
branches.cn: 收割把植株变成了谷粒与面粉。

branches.en: Bread and whisky are the two great products of rye grain.
branches.cn: 面包与威士忌是黑麦谷粒最重要的两种产物。

branches.en: A field of rye is the plant seen as a mass, not as a single stalk.
branches.cn: 黑麦田是把这种植物看成一大片，而不是单株。

branches.en: Flour is the middle step between the grain and the loaf on the table.
branches.cn: 面粉是谷粒与桌上那条面包之间的中间环节。

intro.en: Rye is a short root word with hardly any affixation, so the useful pieces around it are its compounds, not prefixes or suffixes.
intro.cn: rye 是一个几乎没有词缀的短词根，可供分解的不是前后缀，而是围绕它的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Rye is a Germanic word with no Latin source, so the list below names the Old English and Germanic shapes plus the common compounds.
latinIntro.cn: rye 是日耳曼语词，没有拉丁语来源，因此下面列出的是古英语与日耳曼语形态以及常见的复合词。

items.example: Ryge is the Old English shape of rye.
items.exampleCN: ryge 是 rye 的古英语形态。

items.example: The Norse rugr confirms the Germanic root.
items.exampleCN: 诺尔斯语的 rugr 印证了那个日耳曼词根。

items.example: German Roggen is the cousin of rye.
items.exampleCN: 德语的 Roggen 是 rye 的表亲。

items.meaning: a baked food made from flour
items.example: The part bread forms ryebread.
items.exampleCN: 成分 bread 构成 ryebread。

items.example: The part grass forms ryegrass.
items.exampleCN: 成分 grass 构成 ryegrass。

items.example: Whisky follows rye in rye whisky.
items.exampleCN: whisky 紧跟在 rye 后面构成 rye whisky。

items.example: Flour follows rye in rye flour.
items.exampleCN: flour 跟在 rye 后面构成 rye flour。

items.meaning: a grain plant grown for food
items.meaningCN: 作为食物种植的谷物作物
items.example: Rye belongs to the cereal group.
items.exampleCN: 黑麦属于谷物这一类别。

items.example: The two-part name rye grass hides a different plant.
items.exampleCN: 两段式的 rye grass 其实指另一种植物。

definition_zh: 保护；防护；保障措施；安全装置
definition_en: to protect something from harm or risk, or a measure that gives such protection
core_image: 一只手把门闩推紧，把风险挡在门外的动作
scene: 港口的管理员每天检查围栏和监控，防止有人偷偷登船。Each morning the port officer walks the fence line to safeguard the docks.
sceneCN: 这里 safeguard 是「保护、防护」（第 1 个义项：防止某人或某物受到伤害或损失）；句意：港口的管理员每天沿着围栏走一遍，以保护码头安全。

pos.zh: 保障措施；防护措施；安全装置

derivatives.zh: 保护工作；以动词加 -ing 构成的名词，指保护与照管的职责
保管人；由 safe 加 keeper 构成的罕见复合词，指代为保管物品的人

senses.title: To protect from harm
senses.definition: to keep a person, place or system safe from danger or damage
senses.definitionCN: 使人、地方或系统免受危险或损害
senses.example: New rules safeguard workers from toxic fumes.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定保护工人不受有毒烟气伤害。
senses.why: The word is a compound of safe and guard, so the image is a guard standing watch precisely because something is safe.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 safe（安全的）与 guard（看守）的复合，画面就是正因为东西要安全，才需要有人守着。

senses.title: To defend interests or rights
senses.definition: to defend rights, interests or values, often through rules, law or public effort
senses.definitionCN: 通过规定、法律或公共努力维护权利、利益或价值观
senses.example: The treaty safeguards the rights of minority groups.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约保障少数群体的权利。
senses.why: Protection moves from the body to the law: rights are the things that need a guard around them.
senses.whyCN: 保护的对象从身体转到法律：权利正是需要被围护起来的东西。

senses.title: A protective measure
senses.definition: a rule, device or procedure that prevents harm
senses.definitionCN: 防止伤害的规则、装置或程序
senses.example: Helmets are a basic safeguard in construction work.
senses.exampleCN: 安全帽是建筑工作中最基本的防护措施。
senses.why: The noun sense turns the guarding action into a countable thing, a measure that acts as a guard.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把守护的动作变成可以数的一件东西，即平时守着你的那道措施。

senses.title: A safety device
senses.definition: a mechanical part that stops a machine or process when something goes wrong
senses.definitionCN: 机器或流程出错时自动起作用的机械部件
senses.example: The boiler has a pressure safeguard that shuts it off.
senses.exampleCN: 锅炉装有压力安全装置，会自动切断电源。
senses.why: Technology borrows the guarding image and puts it inside a machine as a built-in guard.
senses.whyCN: 技术领域借用了看守的意象，把它装进机器里，成为内置的守卫。

intro.en: Safeguard joins safe, from Latin salvus meaning healthy and unhurt, with the romance verb guard, of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: safeguard 由 safe 与 guard 合成；safe 源于拉丁语 salvus（健全、未受伤），guard 则来自日耳曼语，经由罗曼语传入英语。

items.en: Salvus means safe, healthy and unhurt.
items.cn: salvus 意为安全、健全、未受伤害。

items.en: Sauf carries the sound of salvus and means safe.
items.cn: 古法语 sauf 承接 salvus 的读音，意为安全的。

items.en: The verb guard, of Germanic origin, enters English through French and means to keep watch.
items.cn: 一般认为，源于日耳曼语的动词 guard 经法语进入英语，意为看守、守护。

items.en: Safe and guard are already known separately in English.
items.cn: safe 与 guard 作为独立的词，在英语中已分别出现。

items.en: The compound safeguard appears as a noun and verb and spreads into law and engineering.
items.cn: 复合词 safeguard 以名词与动词的身份出现，并扩展到法律与工程领域。

note.en: Safeguard sits among shield words (protect, defend, shield) and among control nouns (safety, protection, guard).
note.cn: safeguard 一侧连着表示「护住」的动词（protect、defend、shield），另一侧连着表示保障的名词（safety、protection、guard）。

entries.definition: free from danger
entries.definitionCN: 安全的；无危险的（safeguard 的第一部分）

entries.definition: to watch over and protect
entries.definitionCN: 守卫；保卫（safeguard 的第二部分）

entries.definition: protective measures
entries.definitionCN: 各项保障措施；同一个词的复数形式

entries.definition: to keep someone from harm
to place something between a person and harm
to make something safe or certain to last
entries.definitionCN: 使安全；确保；把某物巩固下来

normalIntro.en: Safeguard is literally a safe guard: a watch kept so that something stays safe.
normalIntro.cn: safeguard 字面上就是「一道让东西保持安全的看守」，安全在被守出来的。

normal.en: Split it as safe plus guard to recall both halves.
normal.cn: 拆成 safe 加 guard 两部分来记，两个词各贡献一半意思。

normal.en: Safeguard is both a verb and a noun, so you can do it and also name it.
normal.cn: 它既能当动词也能当名词，所以既能说「去保护」，也能说「一种保障」。

normal.en: Safeguard against something means to build a defense before trouble arrives.
normal.cn: safeguard against 某物，意思是在麻烦到来之前先筑起防线。

normal.en: Its near relatives are guard, protection and safety.
normal.cn: 同族近义词就是 guard、protection 和 safety。

normal.en: Legal and technical texts use safeguards for rights and for machines.
normal.cn: 法律与工程文本里用 safeguards 指权利保障与机器上的保险装置。

abstract.en: See a guard leaning against a door that must stay shut.
abstract.cn: 想象一个守卫靠着那扇必须关住的门。

abstract.en: Picture a signature at the bottom of a contract acting like a fence.
abstract.cn: 想象合同末尾的签名像一圈篱笆一样围住权利。

abstract.en: Think of a valve that closes itself just before pressure becomes dangerous.
abstract.cn: 想象一个阀门在压力变得危险之前自动关上。

examples.en: The company must safeguard customer data.
examples.cn: 公司必须保护客户的资料。

examples.en: Strict checks served as a safeguard against fraud.
examples.cn: 严格的检查起到防范欺诈的作用。

examples.en: Their safeguards failed and the reactor overheated.
examples.cn: 他们的安全装置失灵，反应堆过热了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「safe 塞斧」：把斧子塞进柜子里锁好，就是把它「保护」起来；再联想 guard 的看守。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 salvus（健全、未受伤）→ 古法语 sauf → 英语 safe（安全的）；日耳曼语 *wardōn（看守）经古法语 garde 进入英语成为 guard；两者复合为 safeguard，核心义「把安全看守起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Safeguard starts as the act of protecting, widens to legal and moral defense, then turns into countable measures and finally into a machine part.
sensesIntro.cn: safeguard 从「保护」这一动作出发，扩展到法律与道义上的维护，再变成可数的保障措施，最后落在机器里的安全装置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a heavy bolt into place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把沉重的门闩推到位。

branches.en: The protecting action is the everyday verb sense.
branches.cn: 保护的动作用法是最日常的动词义。

branches.en: Defending rights is the legal and moral extension.
branches.cn: 维护权利是法律与道义层面的延伸。

branches.en: Countable measures and device parts are the noun senses.
branches.cn: 可数的措施与装置部件属于名词义。

branches.en: The verb protects and the noun names the thing that protects.
branches.cn: 动词说的是去保护，名词指的是保护你的那样东西。

branches.en: A legal safeguard is a measure that defends a right.
branches.cn: 法律保障就是用来维护权利的一种措施。

intro.en: Safeguard is a two-part compound: the Latin-rooted safe and the Germanic-rooted guard meet in English.
intro.cn: safeguard 是两部分复合词：拉丁来源的 safe 与日耳曼来源的 guard 在英语里相遇。

latinIntro.en: Latin salvus gives English safe, save and safety; guard is a Germanic word that travelled through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salvus 带来英语的 safe、save 与 safety；guard 则是经法语传入的日耳曼词。

items.example: Safe supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: safe 提供复合词的前一半。

items.example: Guard supplies the watching action.
items.exampleCN: guard 提供「看守」的动作。

items.example: Safeguard carries the main modern sense.
items.exampleCN: safeguard 承载主要现代义。

items.meaning: forming a noun from a verb
items.meaningCN: 把动词变成名词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms safeguarding.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 safeguarding。

items.example: Safeguarding names the duty itself.
items.exampleCN: safeguarding 直接指这项职责本身。

items.example: Safety shares the Latin root of safe.
items.exampleCN: safety 与 safe 共享拉丁词根。

items.example: Save also comes from Latin salvus.
items.exampleCN: save 同样来自拉丁语 salvus。

items.meaning: the act of storing something safely
items.example: Safekeeping repeats the safe element.
items.exampleCN: safekeeping 再次用到 safe 这一部分。

items.example: Safeguarded is the past participle form.
items.exampleCN: safeguarded 是过去分词形式。

definition_zh: 蝾螈；火蜥蜴；传说中不怕火的火精灵
definition_en: a small amphibian with soft moist skin and a long tail, or the creature said in old legends to live in fire
core_image: 一只细长的小两栖动物从湿叶下缓缓爬过，身上闪着水光
scene: 雨后的夜里，男孩翻开潮湿的石头，看见一条细长的小动物贴着地面慢慢爬到阴凉处。Next morning the boy found a salamander under the damp stone and carried it gently back to the pond.
sceneCN: 这里 salamander 是「蝾螈」（第 1 个义项：皮肤湿润、尾巴很长的小型两栖动物）；句意：第二天早上，男孩在潮湿的石头下发现了一只蝾螈，并轻轻把它送回池塘。

pos.zh: 传说中不怕火的火精灵

collocations.zh: 火中的火精灵（传说用法）

derivatives.zh: 蝾螈毒素；由 salamander 加 -in（化学物质后缀）构成，指蝾螈皮肤分泌的有毒成分
蝾螈般的；像火一样耐烧的

senses.title: The amphibian
senses.definition: a small animal with soft moist skin and a long tail, related to frogs but shaped like a lizard
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤柔软湿润、尾长、外形像蜥蜴但与蛙类相近的小型动物
senses.example: Most salamanders must keep their skin wet to breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数蝾螈必须保持皮肤湿润才能呼吸。
senses.why: The Greek name salamandra already names this animal, and its image of hiding in damp places gave the word its lasting core.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 salamandra 本来指的就是这种动物，它躲在阴湿处的形象让这个词的核心义一直保留至今。

senses.title: The fire creature
senses.definition: a legendary creature said to live in fire or to put fire out
senses.definitionCN: 传说中生于火中或能灭火的奇异生物
senses.example: Medieval bestiaries call the salamander a child of fire.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪动物志把火蜥蜴称作火的孩子。
senses.why: Old writers saw lizards crawl out of burning logs, so the name grew a fire meaning that fossilised in legends.
senses.whyCN: 古人看到壁虎从燃烧的木柴里爬出，于是这个名字长出了「火」的含义，并被传说固定下来。

senses.title: Something that endures heat
senses.definition: figuratively, a person or object that survives intense heat, danger or hardship unharmed
senses.definitionCN: 比喻能安然捱过烈焰、危险或困境的人或物
senses.example: The old furnace was the salamander of the steelworks, always burning, never falling.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老炉子堪称钢厂的「火蜥蜴」，永远在燃烧，从不倒下。
senses.why: The fire sense is borrowed again to praise whatever comes through a trial unburnt.
senses.whyCN: 「火」的义项再被借用来称赞那些穿过考验却毫发无损的人或物。

intro.en: Salamander comes from Greek salamandra through Latin and Old French; the ancient Greeks already used it for a newt-like creature.
intro.cn: salamander 由希腊语 salamandra 经拉丁语与古法语传入英语；古希腊人已用它指一种类似蝾螈的生物。

items.en: Salamandra names a small lizard-like creature that lives near water.
items.cn: 希腊语 salamandra 指一种靠近水边生活、形似蜥蜴的小生物。

items.en: Latin keeps salamandra and adds the tale of its fire-proof skin.
items.cn: 拉丁语沿用 salamandra，并附会上它不怕火的传说。

items.en: The word passes through Old French on its way to English.
items.cn: 这个词经由古法语进入英语。

items.en: Salamander appears in English by around the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 一般认为，salamander 在十四世纪前后出现于英语。

items.en: Science fixes the word on the amphibian, while literature keeps the fire creature.
items.cn: 科学把这词固定给两栖动物，文学则保留了火中的精灵。

note.en: Salamander is close to its animal neighbours newt, lizard and eft, and to the story creature of myth.
note.cn: salamander 一边挨着动物邻居 newt、lizard 与 eft，一边连着神话里那种奇异的火中生物。

entries.definition: more than one salamander
relating to salamanders or to fire
shaped like a salamander
entries.definitionCN: 形似蝾螈的；由 salamander 加 -oid 构成的形容词

entries.definition: a small lizard-like amphibian living in water
entries.definitionCN: 水螈；生活在水中的小型两栖动物

entries.definition: a reptile with dry scaly skin
entries.definitionCN: 蜥蜴；皮肤干燥带鳞片的爬行动物

entries.definition: an old English word for the newt
entries.definitionCN: 古英语中对水螈的旧称

normalIntro.en: Salamander borrows an old Greek name for a slippery creature that lives in wet holes.
normalIntro.cn: salamander 借来一个古老的希腊名字，指那种住在潮湿洞穴里、滑溜溜的生物。

normal.en: The ending -ander makes it a creature word you can picture wet and soft.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -ander 让它听起来像一种生物，脑子里能浮现出湿软的样子。

normal.en: Salamander is an amphibian, so it needs water where a lizard does not.
normal.cn: salamander 是两栖动物，需要水，而蜥蜴不需要。

normal.en: In legends the same word means a fire creature, the opposite of its damp real life.
normal.cn: 在传说里同一个词又指火中的生物，正与它现实中潮湿的生活相反。

normal.en: Giant salamander is the big Chinese species, a good fixed phrase to keep.
normal.cn: giant salamander 指大鲵，是一个值得记下的固定搭配。

normal.en: Compare newt and eft, two closer animals that share its cold wet world.
normal.cn: 对比 newt 与 eft，它们都是和它共享寒冷潮湿世界的小动物。

abstract.en: Picture a damp stone lifted at night, with something glistening underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里翻开一块湿石头，下面有东西在发亮。

abstract.en: See a small creature walking into a campfire and walking back out unhurt.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小生物走进篝火，又毫发无损地走出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a blacksmith shouting that the furnace is the real salamander here.
abstract.cn: 想象铁匠大喊，这炉子才是真正的火蜥蜴。

examples.en: A salamander slipped under the wet leaves near the stream.
examples.cn: 一只蝾螈钻进了溪边潮湿的落叶下。

examples.en: Ancient people believed that salamanders could live in fire.
examples.cn: 古人相信火蜥蜴可以生活在火里。

examples.en: The giant salamander is among the largest amphibians on earth.
examples.cn: 大鲵是地球上最大的两栖动物之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沙来满得」：沙地边上的水洼里，滑溜的小生物来得满满当当；这也只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 salamandra（一种近水的蜥形小生物）→ 拉丁语 salamandra → 古法语 → 英语 salamander；希腊语词形内部构成为「来源不确定」，勿强行拆分。核心义「贴地爬行的湿皮小动物」，由此再长出「火中精灵」的传说义。

sensesIntro.en: Salamander begins as a real amphibian, grows a legendary fire sense, and ends as a figure for anything that survives burning.
sensesIntro.cn: salamander 先指真实的两栖动物，再长出传说中的火中精灵义，最后成为「耐得住烈火之物」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long wet body sliding out from under a stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条湿漉漉的长身子从石头底下滑出来。

branches.en: The real amphibian is the first and literal sense.
branches.cn: 真实的两栖动物是最初的字面义。

branches.en: The fire creature is the legendary sense.
branches.cn: 火中的生物是传说义。

branches.en: Anything unburnt by heat is the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 任何不被烧毁之物是比喻义。

branches.en: A humble wet animal becomes a figure for surviving fire.
branches.cn: 一种卑微的湿皮动物，反而成了熬过烈火的象征。

branches.en: The legend of the fire creature directly feeds the figure of speech.
branches.cn: 火中精灵的传说直接孕育了这个比喻用法。

intro.en: Salamander is borrowed whole from Greek; English builds little on it except a few learned names.
intro.cn: salamander 是从希腊语整词借来的，英语除少数书面派生名外几乎不在它上面再构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin simply carries over Greek salamandra and its fire story.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只是照搬希腊语的 salamandra 和它关于火的传说。

items.example: Salamander keeps its Greek core.
items.exampleCN: salamander 保留希腊词的核心义。

items.example: The suffix -s forms salamanders.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成复数 salamanders。

items.example: The suffix -ine forms salamandrine.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ine 构成 salamandrine。

items.example: Salamandrine describes a creature or a fire.
items.exampleCN: salamandrine 可形容生物，也可形容火。

items.example: The suffix -in forms salamandrin.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -in 构成 salamandrin。

items.example: Giant salamander shows the word as a head noun.
items.exampleCN: giant salamander 显示这个词可做中心名词。

items.meaning: a black and yellow European species
items.meaningCN: 火蝾螈（一种黑黄相间的欧洲蝾螈）
items.example: Fire salamander preserves the fire association.
items.exampleCN: fire salamander 保留了与火的联想。

items.example: Salamandroid borrows the -oid ending.
items.exampleCN: salamandroid 借用了 -oid 词尾。

latinEntries.meaning: a lizard-like creature, fabled to live in fire
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一种蜥形生物，传说生活在火中

latinEntries.meaning: an asbestos-like cloth said to be salamander wool
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一种被称为「蝾螈毛」的不燃织物

definition_zh: 三文鱼；鲑鱼；鲑鱼肉；鲑肉粉色
definition_en: a large fish with silver scales and orange pink flesh that swims up rivers to lay its eggs
core_image: 一条银亮的鱼逆着水流跃上石阶，身上泛出橙粉色
scene: 秋天河面泛起凉意，鱼群成群结队往上游游去，要回到出生的浅滩产卵。Every autumn the river fills with salmon swimming upstream to spawn where they were born.
sceneCN: 这里 salmon 是「鲑鱼」（第 1 个义项：银亮的大鱼，会逆流洄游到河流上游产卵）；句意：每年秋天，河中都挤满了逆流而上、回到出生地产卵的鲑鱼。

collocations.zh: 在河里的鲑鱼（洄游语境）

derivatives.zh: 沙门氏菌；命名与 salmon 只是形近，词源上来自人名 Salmon，与鲑鱼无关
鲑鱼一样的；由 salmon 加 -ey 构成的少见形容词，指肉质或颜色像鲑鱼的

senses.title: The fish
senses.definition: a large fish with silver scales whose flesh is orange pink, famous for swimming up rivers
senses.definitionCN: 鳞片银亮、肉呈橙粉色的大型鱼，以逆流洄游著称
senses.example: The salmon were crowded at the foot of the waterfall.
senses.exampleCN: 鲑鱼挤在瀑布脚下。
senses.why: The word came from Latin salmo by way of French, and old writers linked it to sal, so a salt fish became simply the fish.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由拉丁语 salmo 经法语而来，古人又把它与 sal（盐）联系起来，于是「咸水鱼」最终就成了这种鱼的名字。

senses.title: The food
senses.definition: the flesh of this fish eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 这种鱼的肉，作为食物
senses.example: We had grilled salmon with new potatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 我们吃了烤鲑鱼配新土豆。
senses.why: Talking of a fish often slides into talking of it on a plate, which is the everyday food sense.
senses.whyCN: 谈鱼往往滑向谈餐盘上的鱼，这就成为最日常的「鱼肉」义。

senses.title: The colour
senses.definition: an orange pink like the flesh of the fish
senses.definitionCN: 近似鲑鱼肉色的橙粉色
senses.example: She painted the bedroom in a soft salmon.
senses.exampleCN: 她把卧室刷成了柔和的鲑肉粉色。
senses.why: The flesh is a memorable colour, so the fish name doubles as a colour name.
senses.whyCN: 鲑鱼肉的颜色太好记，于是鱼名同时成了颜色名。

intro.en: Salmon goes back to Latin salmo, which is of uncertain origin, and reached English through French with its L no longer sounded.
intro.cn: salmon 源自拉丁语 salmo，其内部构成「来源不确定」；它经法语进入英语，这里有一个 L 音早已不再发音。

items.en: Salmo names the fish; its forming elements are unknown.
items.cn: salmo 指这种鱼，其内部构词成分来源不确定。

items.en: Some writers guessed a link with sal, salt, but this is popular rather than proved.
items.cn: 有些古代作者猜测它与 sal（盐）有关，但这只是民间说法，未获证实。

items.en: Saumon is the form that crosses into English.
items.cn: 古法语 saumon 是进入英语的形式。

items.en: The word is spelled with an L that Latin brought back into the spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语的拼写中重新出现了 L，这是拉丁语拼写影响的痕迹。

items.en: The L is still written but not pronounced, and salmon also names a colour.
items.cn: 这个 L 至今只写不读；salmon 另外又成了一种植物的颜色名。

note.en: Salmon sits with the other river fish (trout, char, eel) and with its near-homophone salmonella.
note.cn: salmon 一边与其他河鱼（trout、char、eel）同场，一边连着与它形近音近的 salmonella。

entries.definition: a bacterium that causes food poisoning
entries.definitionCN: 引起食物中毒的沙门氏菌，只是与 salmon 拼写相近，词源上来自人名 Salmon，两者词源不同

entries.definition: a less common plural of the fish name
entries.definitionCN: 较少用的复数形式，多数场合复数仍写 salmon

entries.definition: the French word for salmon
entries.definitionCN: 法语中的鲑鱼一词，英语 salmon 的直接来源，两者同根

entries.definition: a speckled freshwater fish of the same family
entries.definitionCN: 鳟鱼；与鲑鱼同科的带斑点淡水鱼

entries.definition: a cold-water fish of the salmon family
entries.definitionCN: 红点鲑；鲑科的一种冷水鱼

entries.definition: a long snake-like fish that also migrates
entries.definitionCN: 鳗鱼；同样有洄游习性的细长鱼

normalIntro.en: Salmon is a fish name with a silent L and an old French shape behind it.
normalIntro.cn: salmon 是一个带「默音 L」的鱼名，背后有古法语的影子。

normal.en: The L in salmon is written but never spoken.
normal.cn: salmon 里的 L 只写不读。

normal.en: Salmon is countable but usually stays salmon in the plural.
normal.cn: 它可数，但复数通常仍写作 salmon。

normal.en: Smoked salmon is the phrase you will see on most menus.
normal.cn: smoked salmon 是菜单上最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Salmon farming and salmon run are fixed phrases in the news.
normal.cn: salmon farming 与 salmon run 是新闻里的固定说法。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with salmonella, a germ named after a person.
normal.cn: 不要与 salmonella 混淆，那是以人名命名的细菌。

abstract.en: Watch a silver body leap over a wall of white water.
abstract.cn: 看着一条银色的身子跃过一堵白色的水墙。

abstract.en: See a plate of pink fish beside a slice of lemon.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘粉色的鱼肉，旁边配一片柠檬。

abstract.en: Paint a wall in the soft pink the fish flesh leaves you thinking of.
abstract.cn: 把一面墙刷成鱼肉留下的那种柔和粉色。

examples.en: Salmon swim hundreds of miles back to their birthplace.
examples.cn: 鲑鱼游数百英里回到出生地。

examples.en: She ordered a salad with smoked salmon on top.
examples.cn: 她点了一份上面铺着烟熏三文鱼的沙拉。

examples.en: The sunset left the sky a pale salmon.
examples.cn: 夕阳把天空染成了淡淡的鲑肉粉色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三文鱼」正是 salmon 在中文里的常用名，「萨门」的读法也贴近音标；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 salmo（鲑鱼）→ 古法语 saumon → 中古英语 salmon；拉丁语 salmo 的内部构成为「来源不确定」，旧时与 sal（盐）的联系属民间说法；核心义「逆流而上的银亮大鱼」。

sensesIntro.en: Salmon moves from the living fish to its flesh on a plate and then to the colour of that flesh.
sensesIntro.cn: salmon 从活着的鱼，转到餐盘上的鱼肉，再转成那种鱼肉的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver fish leaping up the rapids.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条银鱼跃上湍急的水流。

branches.en: The living fish is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 活鱼是首要义项。

branches.en: The edible flesh is the food sense.
branches.cn: 可食用的鱼肉是食物义项。

branches.en: The orange pink shade is the colour sense.
branches.cn: 橙粉色是颜色义项。

branches.en: Naming the fish and naming the dish on the menu are the same word.
branches.cn: 指称这种鱼与指称菜单上的菜，用的是同一个词。

branches.en: The colour takes its very name from the flesh of the food.
branches.cn: 这种颜色的名字直接取自食物的肉色。

intro.en: Salmon is a borrowed fish name with no living affixes; English mainly fixes its spelling and adds a few compounds.
intro.cn: salmon 是个借来的鱼名，没有活用的词缀；英语主要在它的拼写上做文章，并组成若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin salmo is the remote ancestor, though its own parts cannot be recovered with confidence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salmo 是它的远祖，但 salmo 自身的构词部分已无法可靠复原。

items.meaning: a fish of the family Salmonidae
items.example: Salmon is unchanged in the plural.
items.exampleCN: salmon 复数形式不变。

items.example: Smoked salmon is a common compound.
items.exampleCN: smoked salmon 是常见的复合词。

items.meaning: a place where salmon are raised
items.example: Salmon farm names the place of production.
items.exampleCN: salmon farm 指养殖场所。

items.meaning: a pink berry of the northwestern coast of America
items.meaningCN: 美洲西北海岸的一种粉色浆果
items.example: Salmonberry shows salmon used before a noun.
items.exampleCN: salmonberry 显示 salmon 可放在名词前作修饰成分。

items.example: The suffix -oid could form salmonoid.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -oid 可构成 salmonoid。

items.example: Salmonoid describes a similar fish.
items.exampleCN: salmonoid 形容相似的鱼。

items.example: Salmonidae is the scientific family name.
items.exampleCN: Salmonidae 是科学上的科名。

items.meaning: another name for the sea trout
items.example: Salmon trout is an older compound.
items.exampleCN: salmon trout 是较早的复合词。
